decision_journal.decision: Built recoverMissingOhlcvSession() + runOhlcvCandlePresenceGuard() net-new (sibling ALPHA-S1-CANDLE-RECOVER closed false-positive, shipped no code, so its shared primitive never existed). Calendar-aware via vnTradingCalendar's new mostRecentTradingDayOnOrBefore() (bounded 14-day backward walk over isVnTradingDay) — structurally prevents ever treating a weekend/holiday as a missing session. Wired at startup (static import) + trailing inside runOhlcvDailyAggregator itself (checks the PREVIOUS trading day via nowMs-24h, dynamic import to avoid a static circular import back through this same file). Fixed a real arithmetic bug in the architect design doc's illustrative re-aggregation snippet (nowMs must be end-of-VN-session, not midnight+5h, else the afternoon close is silently dropped from the recovered candle) — disclosed in commit message, not a re-architecture. Fail-loud does not invent a new retry ladder: a persistent gap that routes through VPS-relay is escalated by the ALREADY-EXISTING R-5 ladder in handleOhlcvBackfillDone (sibling commit 599f4aee0) once the poller reports back. Commit 1bbc8cead, disjoint file set from the sibling row. Moved in_progress->review, deploy_pending:true, top-level .head synced to next_agent:qa.
decision_journal.what_considered: (A) implement recoverMissingOhlcvSession per the architect's §1 snippet verbatim, including the nowMs=midnight+5h re-aggregation window — REJECTED after a direct unit test (3 ticks spanning the full VN session) showed the aggregator's own window is [vnMidnight(nowMs), nowMs), so +5h truncates capture to the pre-market hours and silently drops the actual session close; would have shipped a recovery path that produces a wrong candle while looking correct. (B) leave the trailing daily-aggregator call site as a static import of ohlcvCandleGuard.ts — REJECTED: creates a 3-node static circular import (ohlcvDailyAggregatorJob -> ohlcvCandleGuard -> recoverMissingOhlcvSession -> ohlcvDailyAggregatorJob); used a dynamic import instead, mirroring the deferred-load idiom ohlcvStartupProbe.ts already uses for the same reason. (C) add a bespoke retry-cap/escalation ladder inside the guard itself for a persistent gap — REJECTED per the task's explicit instruction to reuse the existing ladder, not invent a new one: the VPS-relay branch's ohlcv_backfill_queue insert already flows into the sibling's already-fixed R-5 ladder.
decision_journal.why_change: Architect design (docs/handoffs/ALPHA-S1-architect-design.md §1/§2) is the design authority and was followed for orchestration/branch structure/interfaces verbatim; the one deviation (aggregation-window arithmetic) is a correctness bug-fix within the design's own illustrative code, not a scope or architecture change, and is fully disclosed in the commit message and notebook.

No other row in this table embeds a fenced/multi-line block below it, so no direct precedent existed; chose Option 2 (qa's own flagged safer option) as the spec-compliant fix.

The candidate mechanisms differ sharply in blast radius, and a fleet-wide hard-reject pre-commit hook chosen by an unattended generic developer via zone-detect's Tier-3 fallback is the specific bad outcome: a misfiring hard-reject blocks every agent and every human on the repo. A design gate is worth the cost of manual dispatch here. (D) Mandate fail-closed on the guard, citing UC-CRITIC-HOOKS-ENFORCEMENT — REJECTED as overreach into design AND as wrong on the merits: fail-closed on a PRE-COMMIT hook IS the fleet-outage risk. The defect that row documents is SILENCE (`2>/dev/null || true` makes a crashed validator look like a pass), not leniency. MINTED: FIX-PDFX-TESSERACT-CONCURRENCY-VIOLATES-SINGLE-WORKER-INVARIANT (P0, zone apps/pdf-extractor/, next_agent=architect, plan_only, supervised) — verified present in .task_board.backlog. MECHANISM FOUND, which is what the earlier ruling lacked and why it declined to mint: pdf-extractor is running TEN concurrent tesseract processes against a code-declared, code-commented, unit-tested single-worker invariant (apps/pdf-extractor/main.py:154 `ocr_executor = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)` commented 'no parallel Tesseract processes on the 16GB Mac — matches PekEngineAdapter Semaphore(1)'; interface/handlers.py:451 'PekEngineAdapter uses threading.Semaphore(1). Triage as ONE'. The dedup gate behaved correctly. entries.vision: Make /dashboard/prediction-claims update DAILY, not weekly. User: page not update many day, wants update continue day by day. ROOT CAUSE (router RAW-confirmed + PO-verified live): page + /api/prediction-claims + predictionClaimsHandler are HEALTHY — do NOT touch them. The DATA PRODUCER is starved: prediction_claims has only 9 rows, newest 2026-06-14 (agentId 08-prediction-synthesizer). The synthesis flow (digest-predict/flow/monday.md, P-3..P-5 create_prediction_claim) was DISABLED by Sprint 1949-T5 (Monday prediction synthesis removed — Sunday weekly covers full scope); the Sunday weekly.md flow only READS get_prediction_accuracy, it never calls create_prediction_claim. So NO active flow has produced a claim since 1949-T5 — the 06-14 batch was the last routed run. Live confirm: get_prediction_accuracy(30d)=no results; calibration Brier=0.1379 healthy (product is SOUND, just unfed).
entries.product_decision: Option (a) chosen: re-enable prediction synthesis on a DAILY cadence by routing digest-predict to a daily prediction sub-flow + a new daily cowork slot, WITHOUT disturbing the Sunday weekly calibration report. Daily update = a daily synthesis run that CREATES new high-conviction claims when fresh evidence appears AND lets existing open claims keep accruing toward their multi-day/weekly horizon (e.g. W26). It is NOT a forced 5-claims-every-day spam. GUARDRAILS (designed by architect first): (1) per-DAY cap (small, e.g. 2-3) replacing the monday max_prediction_claims_per_week:5, with a weekly ceiling so cadence cannot inflate claim volume; (2) same-day idempotency marker via task_claim (TTL ~20h) keyed on day+slot so a re-fire never double-creates; (3) NO-OP cleanly when no ticker passes the bullish/bearish>0.6 high-conviction filter (do NOT lower the bar to manufacture daily claims — standing no-fake-data directive); (4) Sunday weekly.md calibration report stays unchanged + un-regressed.
entries.success_metric: LIVE: prediction_claims gains new rows on consecutive (high-conviction) days; /dashboard/prediction-claims generatedAt + rows reflect them day-over-day; daily/weekly caps honored; flat-market day no-ops without fabricating claims; Sunday weekly MARKET calibration dish still fires unchanged. entries.root_cause: PROVEN on two planes. (1) The host —France/CEST— lost its caffeinate wake-lock at ~05:00-05:13Z (pmset: multiple `caffeinate ClientDied`) when the interactive CLI session holding the */15 CronCreate cowork dispatcher ended; the host then entered standby/darkwake. (2) The launchd StartInterval guaranteed-slot firer provably did NOT execute for ~11.5h (05:58Z->17:34Z): the firer logs a line whenever it MATCHES a guaranteed slot, and chef-eod(08:45Z)+fb-daily(09:15Z) had last_fired=07-21 which does NOT suppress them, so had launchd run the firer in-window it WOULD have logged+fired them — their total absence from the 07-22 log proves StartInterval never ran (host not rebooted: uptime 11d; job not unloaded: resumed same-day 17:34Z). Both coverage planes were dark. On resume at 17:34Z the matcher only offers slots within +/-2min of the CURRENT nominal tick — the 08:45/09:00/09:15/11:00/14:00Z windows were hours gone and NEVER re-offered. `guaranteed:true` is therefore a false promise across any host-standby/session-down window: neither plane has look-back/catch-up.
entries.vision: Make cowork `guaranteed:true` an HONORED contract, not a false promise. A guaranteed slot whose firing window elapsed while the host was in standby or the session was down must, on the next live tick/startup, either be recovered exactly once within a bounded freshness-safe catch-up window, OR record a structured (non-silent) miss when the VN trading day has already rolled past its window — and the `guaranteed` label must be corrected wherever it overstates real coverage.
entries.scope_in: TRACK A (PRIMARY, dev-team chain): add look-back/catch-up to the guaranteed-slot firing path shared by all 3 callers (scripts/agents-flow/cowork-match-slots.js matcher, scripts/agents-flow/cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer.sh launchd firer, and the live */15 dispatcher startup). On each tick/startup, in addition to the +/-2min current-tick match, detect guaranteed slots DUE earlier in the current VN trading day but never fired (last_fired < today scheduled-fire epoch) and re-offer them IF now is within a bounded, per-dish-type catch-up window that keeps the deliverable meaningful (tight for market/FB posts, looser for chef/digest). Dedup STRICTLY via the existing published:<slot_id>:<VN-work-date> task_claim marker so a late catch-up never double-posts and never labels stale data as fresh. VN-date rollover is explicit: if the VN day rolled past the slot window, DO NOT retro-post under a new date — skip + record miss. CONSOLIDATES the existing cluster (subsume together, do NOT re-litigate): SPIKE-DEAD-WINDOW-20260722-EIGHT-HOUR-SILENCE (root-caused by this triage — its `already_ruled_out: machine sleep` note is INCORRECT, corrected here), SPIKE-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-SUPERSEDE-WIRING (root-caused), FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION (the 07-22 chef-morning exit_code=143 SIGTERM at the 1800s bound / 600s subagent kill truncates guaranteed dishes — catch-up re-firing must complete, not re-truncate), FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-DUAL-PLANE-DOUBLE-FIRE (catch-up adds a 3rd fire path — published-marker arbitration must be verified airtight), FIX-COWORK-LASTFIRED-DECOUPLE-FROM-DELIVERY (catch-up detects a miss via last_fired, so last_fired MUST reflect DELIVERY not just spawn-dispatch). DOC-HONESTY: update cowork-schedule.json `guaranteed` semantics + docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/*.md + docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-07-cowork-guaranteed-slot-durability.md + docs/protocols/cowork-master-cron-runbook.md to state the true coverage envelope.

entries.vision: When any frontend data surface goes stale AT REST, the system automatically DECIDES the root cause and ROUTES a remediation: mint a dev FIX task if the fetch/writer CODE is broken, OR call the responsible refresh agent (market-watcher / news-scout / the cron fetchers) to re-run if the data merely wasn't refreshed — with NO alert spam. This is the auto-REMEDIATE layer (conceptually FFT-L6) sitting ON TOP of L4 detection. Detection already exists and emits SLA-breach signals, but today they DEAD-END: alert-commander suppresses freshness-sla-monitor urgent_news every cycle as infra noise (DS-OBS-01-FIX note in freshnessSlaMonitorJob.ts lines 538-548), so a genuine stale-page breach never mints a fix and never re-runs a fetcher — the user's 'many frontend pages show non-updated data' persists because the signal has no remediation consumer.
entries.scope_in: THREE genuinely-new pieces ON TOP of L4: (1) REMEDIATION-TRIAGE decision-layer — for each breaching surface, read its coverage-map .writer + .cadence, probe the writer's live runtime (generalize queryBctcPipelineRuntimeState's queueDepth+serviceActive idle-vs-crash reader across ALL coverage-map surfaces, not just bctc), and CLASSIFY broken-code (writer service down / erroring / never-scheduled) vs not-refreshed (writer healthy+idle, just didn't run) → route to dev FIX vs refresh-agent re-invoke. (2) ANTI-SPAM gating — REUSE apps/alert-engine dedup-key-builder + cooldown-gate primitives (Go) plus the existing sla_breach_audit 60-min cooldown table; key dedup by (surface, breach-class); SUPPRESS repeat signals while a remediation task/signal is already OPEN for that surface; keep the isVnMarketHours() market-hours gate. (3) ORCHESTRATION integration — REDIRECT the breach signal OFF the dead-end alert-commander addressee ONTO the po/dev-team signal_queue drain (the existing anomaly→BACKLOG bridge: emit-audit-signal.sh + po-s* drain-mint jq library) so remediation is AUTO-picked-up, not a dead alert. Detection-completeness input: coverageMapFreshnessChecker.ts currently maps only 5 of 50 surfaces to DB queries (ENDPOINT_DB_QUERY) — the other 45 are silently skipped, so 'many pages' cannot even be detected yet; widening endpoint→DB coverage is an input the architect must scope for the triage layer to be effective.

entries.success_metric: A forced real breach on a watched surface (a) is CLASSIFIED broken-code-vs-not-refreshed by a live runtime probe (RAW: scheduler log shows the classification), (b) produces EITHER a minted dev FIX task in task_board.backlog (broken-code) OR a re-invoke call to the named refresh agent (not-refreshed) — verified live, not self-report, (c) does NOT re-emit while that remediation is still OPEN (dedup/cooldown proven by a second tick producing no duplicate), (d) the breach signal lands in the po/dev-team signal_queue drain, NOT the suppressed alert-commander path. DoD gate is RAW live evidence per each, not unit-test-only.
entries.product_decision: PO decision: COMPANION sprint, NOT widening FIX-L4. L4 stays the 'does the detector fire + emit' gate (READY, dev-mcp-server, about to execute); this sprint owns 'what happens when it fires'. Widening L4 would bloat a verify-live FIX into a multi-week build and risk the health-recheck stale-duplicate footgun. First concrete step is an architect SPIKE (design-gated) because the broken-code-vs-not-refreshed classifier is genuine technical design (PO not_my_job). Implementation tasks are decomposed by architect/PM/BA AFTER the spike — mint minimally now.

backlog.title: PUBLISHED-MARKER LIFECYCLE — one marker-gate skill, publish-state-conditioned immunity; wire into the 6 copy-pasted gates (P0: caused CONFIRMED user-visible MARKET double-publish 2026-07-15 ids 932+933)
backlog.note:
P0-PROMOTED 2026-07-15T20:06Z by po from signal cow-20260715T195545 (CONFIRMED user-visible double publish, MARKET ids 932+933). UMBRELLA — folds FIX-CHEF-PUBLISHED-MARKER-RELEASE + FU-CHEF-MARKER-INFLOW; both set BLOCKED on this row. THEY MUST NOT SHIP INDEPENDENTLY — independent point patches provably OSCILLATE: 07-02 marker released post-publish -> double publish; 07-03 remediation said release-on-every-no-post-exit -> marker LEAKED on silent exit, suppressing legit dishes; 07-15 an agent complied with the 07-03 rule and released after a REAL publish -> double publish again. The two memory lessons feedback_chef_leaks_published_marker_on_silent_exit (release it!) and feedback-chef-releases-published-marker-enables-peer-double-publish (never release it!) are in DIRECT CONTRADICTION and are auto-injected into agent context — so ANY prose-only fix is non-deterministic by construction. ROOT CAUSE (deeper than the release itself): chef.md claims the marker at Step 0.5 line 32, ~650 lines and one full expensive gather/synthesis BEFORE send_telegram. Claiming before the publish decision is what forces a conditional-release rule, and agents get that conditional wrong in BOTH directions. Note the existing UC-CCA-P3 clause mandatory release-on-no-publish is INSUFFICIENT — it encodes the 07-03 half of the pendulum only. REQUIRED INVARIANT (the WHAT — architect/ba own the HOW): marker release-immunity MUST be a function of publish-state, not of agent prose. Publish SUCCEEDED -> marker is an immutable tombstone, TTL is the ONLY expiry path. Publish NOT attempted/failed -> marker must not survive. PO DESIGN RECOMMENDATION (non-binding, architect decides): two-phase gate — (1) early cheap READ-ONLY probe task_list_held(task_id=MARKER_KEY) at Step 0.5 to abort before burning the pipeline, claiming NOTHING so a leak is impossible; (2) task_claim immediately before send_telegram, claimed:false -> EXIT without sending, claimed:true -> send -> NEVER release. Late-claim makes conditional-release logic unnecessary while the early probe preserves the cost optimisation the current early-claim was reaching for. AC-CODE-GATE (assess, do not assume): prose gates have now failed 3x — evaluate a code-enforced backstop at the releaseTask() choke point in apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/system/coordinationTools.ts (single choke point, also guard task_force_release_orphan) refusing release of task_id matching ^published: . Prefer a task_id-prefix guard over a new task_kind enum value: published: markers and cron: election locks TODAY share task_kind cowork-slot with opposite semantics (dispatch-claim SKILL.md §3.1 table literally documents TTL never released vs explicit release at dispatch end for the same kind), and adding an enum member has a known drift class (feedback_preclaim_gate_taskkind_enum_drift: Zod enum + SQLite CHECK + call sites). ALSO IN SCOPE: chef.md Step 0.5 omits owner_client_session entirely — a violation of spawn-fanout.md L56 (REQUIRED, P1-FINAL TASK_1980) and an unfixed repeat of 07-03 defect #2. AC: (1) invariant holds for both single-fire (TTL 100800) and multi-fire (TTL=cadence) slots; (2) a silent/no-post exit leaves NO marker; (3) a successful publish leaves a marker no agent can release; (4) all 6 copy-pasted gates wired to the one skill; (5) RAW-verify via task_list_held after a real evening dish — marker MUST still be held.

  - emitPressureStateTool.ts:387 stores `args.calendar_status ?? "unknown"`. calendar_status is CALLER-SUPPLIED. The server never computes it and can never itself emit "closed" — its only self-generated value is "unknown".

Whatever literal enters the file once persists forever. THE FILENAME IS NOT GUESSED FROM NOTHING — IT IS RENDERED FROM THE STORED PERIOD KEY. apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:224 calls normaliseFilename(sourceUrl, actionCode, periodYear, periodQuarter), and apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/resolvePdfText.ts:45-61 returns canonical ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf unless the source URL's own basename both ends in .pdf and already contains the action code. So the canonical filename is a faithful projection of financial_reports.period_year/period_quarter — the two cannot disagree, and today the filename is the ONLY place a wrong period identity is visible to a human reading a directory listing.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S DELIVERABLE. "Derive the real filename from source metadata instead of pattern-guessing" is a reasonable goal on its own terms, but it decouples the filename from the stored period. If the stored period is wrong, the file would then be named correctly while the DB row remains mislabelled — the corruption becomes invisible instead of fixed. The live case that prompted this: report_id 5b0dad71-3b05-4455-9823-c2072442777d is stored as DPM_2025_Q4.pdf while its refined content is unambiguously Q1-2026 across five independent pages. The filename is what exposed it.

SEQUENCING RULE, NOT A SCOPE CHANGE: FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT (backlog/P1) must land FIRST. That row adds the period-vs-content validation the ingest boundary has never had (bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:194-201 validates only that the year is 2000..2099 and the quarter is one of Q1..Q4 — shape, never correspondence). Once a wrong period identity cannot be stored, decoupling the filename from it is safe and this row becomes a clean improvement. Until then, this row's change would delete the tripwire.

ADD TO THIS ROW'S ACCEPTANCE when it is eventually worked: a real-filename derivation must not be able to mask a period mismatch — either it preserves a period assertion somewhere visible, or the validation row has already landed. Priority and scope otherwise unchanged (P3/backlog); this is a dependency note, not a promotion.

po 2026-07-25T17:00:10Z — BINDING GATE ADDED. Supersedes the decorative guard po attached at 16:49Z.

WHAT WAS WRONG. At 16:49Z po wrote `blocks: ["FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES"]` onto FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT and treated that as a sequencing guard. IT WAS NOT ONE. The dev-team 16:37Z tick caught it and po re-verified at source: scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:133-141 `effective_depends_on` reads ONLY the CANDIDATE row's own `.depends_on` + `.depends` + `.blocked_by` (inline first; falling back to backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows). It never traverses a reverse `blocks` edge from another row. `deps_satisfied` (:161-164) then short-circuits `true` on an empty list. A full grep of scripts/lib/*.jq, scripts/devteam-*.jq, scripts/orch-*.mjs, scripts/orch-*.sh and scripts/agents-flow/*.sh confirms `blocks` is READ BY NOTHING anywhere in the repo — the only textual hits are unrelated test prose ("blocks idle"). This row therefore carried NO dependency at all in either plane (board row and the backlog-detail.json entry both had depends_on/depends/blocked_by = null), and with supervised/plan_only/owner/next_agent all null, status BACKLOG and no children, it was FULLY BOUNDED-1 ELIGIBLE. Only its P3 rank was holding it back, and rank is queue position, not a guard.

WHAT IS NOW TRUE. `depends_on: ["FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT"]` is written INLINE on this board row. Inline is the binding location by construction: `effective_depends_on` takes inline when non-empty and only consults backlog-detail.json when inline is empty. The gate's own semantics work in this row's favour on both axes — per the code comments at :159-164, a dep is satisfied ONLY when it resolves to `DONE_VERIFIED` (plain `DONE` is NOT sufficient), and a dep id found in NO lane is treated as UNSATISFIED (conservative-skip). The blocker is currently backlog/BACKLOG, so this row is gated until the period-validation fix is genuinely verified, not merely marked done.

WHY IT IS WORTH A REAL GATE AND NOT A COMMENT. Shipping this row alone does not merely fail to help — it makes things worse. The filename is RENDERED from the stored period key (bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:224 -> resolvePdfText.ts:45-61, canonical `ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf`), so today it is the only place a wrong period identity is visible to a human reading a directory listing. Deriving "real" filenames from source metadata decouples the two: a mislabelled row would then be named correctly while the corruption persists, invisibly. That is symptom deletion, and it is exactly what a decorative guard would have permitted.

THE REVERSE `blocks` EDGE IS DELIBERATELY RETAINED on the blocker row as human-readable documentation of intent. It is not load-bearing and must not be relied on. The systemic problem — that `blocks` reads as a constraint while binding nothing — is now owned by FIX-ORCHSTATE-BLOCKS-FIELD-WRITE-ONLY-DECORATIVE (backlog/P2).

It is not safe: the 240-min generic default silently REPLACES the slot's declared weekend rate (gatherer-standard 480, bctc-offmarket 1440), over-firing non-guaranteed slots by up to ~5 extra runs per weekend day, with the slot's declared policy bypassed and nothing logged.

THE CORRECTED DISTINCTION: unmatched-rule-in-real-policy is safe ONLY when the unmatched axis VALUE is itself in-domain (a legitimate combination the table simply does not enumerate). An OUT-OF-DOMAIN axis value — calendar_status="closed" against the file's 5-value domain {open, half_day, weekend, holiday, unknown} — is a CONFIG ERROR wearing the unmatched-rule costume, and must take the fail-loud path, not the 240 default.

Add a DOMAIN check on the VALUE axes: every literal the dispatcher can emit for calendar_status (and any other policy-matching axis) MUST be a member of that axis's value set in cadence-policy.json; fail loud on miss instead of silently absorbing it into the 240 default.

A three-valued direction classifier has silently become a constant that still reports a verdict on every call, and consumers cannot distinguish "the model assessed the rate and found it bearish" from "the model can only say bearish". news-scout emitted "USDVND 26130 bearish >25000 threshold" from it in both c199 and c200 today.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — THE STATED GOAL IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. "Pick one SSOT" does not fix saturation if the value picked is 25000, and 25000 is the most likely pick precisely because it is the one with a named exported constant in Go. Shipping a single-SSOT refactor on 25000 would close this row while leaving the classifier constant — and would additionally propagate the saturated threshold to the two planes (25500 in macroTools.ts / macroAdjustments.ts) that are currently, by accident, slightly less wrong. AC ADDITION, mandatory: whatever value is chosen, add a test asserting that BOTH the bullish and bearish branches remain reachable at the CURRENT live rate, not at a fixture rate. A classifier whose test suite only exercises synthetic inputs cannot detect that its live input has left the discriminating range.

THE DURABLE FIX IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE OF THRESHOLD, AND THAT DECISION BELONGS TO WHOEVER WORKS THIS ROW. A fixed absolute threshold on a drifting nominal exchange rate saturates eventually by construction — this is not a mis-set constant, it is a design that has a shelf life. Honest options: [a] make the threshold relative (z-score or percent deviation against a trailing window, so the discriminating range travels with the series); [b] keep absolute levels but bind them to a real policy anchor (e.g. the SBV reference-rate band) that is itself revised, and add a staleness alarm on the anchor; [c] keep 25000 as a deliberate permanent red-line and DELETE the NEUTRAL/BULLISH branches plus the "direction classifier" framing, so the output honestly reads as a single boolean threshold breach rather than an assessment. What is NOT acceptable is shipping one SSOT and leaving three branches of which two are unreachable. po did not choose among these.

That SPIKE does NOT own this fix; this row does. Priority and scope otherwise unchanged.

What it LACKS is arm (b2): with NO prior row it proceeds to INSERT a brand-new row whose totalAssets is a hardcoded 0 (line 307, bound into the INSERT at line 535), inside an entire all-zeros balance sheet at lines 304-313. Identical defect shape to the one just fixed in storeReport(): refuses to overwrite a good row, but freely CREATES a fresh zero-total row that bctcIdentityGuard.ts then reads at serve time as the OCR-corruption fingerprint. The file's own comment at lines 254-263 already says it 'carried the same two defects' and 'mirrors the identical guard' — the mirror was completed for only one of the two arms.
backlog.po_verified_at_source_20260721T1811: PO RE-READ THE FILE THIS TICK rather than accepting QA's or router's description, and the single decisive fact checks out: `totalAssets: 0` at line 307 is a hardcoded LITERAL and is the ONLY assignment to that field in the whole file (grep: refs at 73, 255, 307, 425, 535 — 307 is the sole write, 535 binds it to the INSERT, 425 is the SQL column list, 255 is the comment, 73 is the summary formatter). There is NO code path in this function that can produce a non-zero balance sheet. The surrounding lines 304-313 are likewise all-zero literals across currentAssets, nonCurrentAssets, liabilities, equity and totalLiabilitiesAndEquity.
backlog.product_question_decide_before_scoping: ANSWER THIS FIRST — the fix does not follow from the defect. Question as router framed it: if a news-inference fallback only ever produces directional hints and never real balance-sheet figures, is writing it into financial_reports — the table bctcIdentityGuard treats as authoritative at serve time — the actual design error, such that guarding arm (b2) alone merely relocates the problem? PO'S STRONG STEER, WITH THE PROOF: YES, IT IS THE DESIGN ERROR, and here is the reductio that settles it. Arm (b1) already blocks every write where a good row exists. Arm (b2), applied literally, blocks every write where NO row exists AND totalAssets<=0. Since totalAssets is hardcoded 0 on EVERY call (verified above — no path produces otherwise), the two arms together block 100% of this function's writes. Adding arm (b2) does not fix the function; it silently converts it into a total no-op while leaving ~600 lines of live, tested, maintained code in place pretending to be a working fallback. A guard that makes its own subject unreachable is not a guard — it is proof that the write target is wrong. CORROBORATING, AND THE PART THAT MAKES THIS USER-FACING RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: (i) the code's OWN comment at lines 254-259 already concedes the whole argument — 'this fallback ALWAYS writes totalAssets=0 ... it reconstructs directional hints from news signals, never real balance-sheet figures — i.e. every call is, by construction, the exact OCR-corruption fingerprint bctcIdentityGuard.ts checks for at serve time.' The codebase has already diagnosed itself; nobody drew the conclusion. (ii) The write is strictly WORSE than not writing, because it destroys an honest signal: an absent row serves 'Chua co du lieu BCTC' ('we do not have this'), whereas a zeros row serves '[CORRUPT DATA - SKIP] total_assets=0 (OCR extraction failure)' — a false claim that we HAVE the filing and it is broken, which misattributes a defect to the filer. This is the same family of harm as the ngay_nop flip on the parent row: fabricating a state that defames a real-world filing. (iii) buildAnalysisSummary() at line 73 formats this into Vietnamese RAG-retrievable prose — 'Tong tai san: 0 trieu dong.' — a flat factual assertion that the company has zero total assets, written into the retrieval corpus. That is fabricated financial data in a served surface, and it engages feedback_no_fake_data_real_fetch directly. THEREFORE the design target to evaluate is: directional news-inference hints belong in a hints/signals surface, NOT in financial_reports. BA must still evaluate the alternatives honestly (a separate table/column; a nullable-financials sentinel row explicitly marked non-authoritative that bctcIdentityGuard excludes; or deleting the write path entirely and keeping the function as a pure read-side hint producer) — my steer is not a pre-selected implementation, and if BA finds a consumer that genuinely needs these rows in financial_reports, say so and I will revisit.

backlog.title: 'Write acceptance criteria before editing files' is structurally unverifiable for every agent whose commit zone excludes orch-state.json — move acceptance authorship to the dispatcher
backlog.po_evidence: Surfaced by the FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD-SKILLS supervised sign-off 2026-07-21. agent-father claimed it wrote acceptance onto the row BEFORE editing any file, and the row carries self-reported acceptance_written_at=2026-07-21T19:08:10Z. But the acceptance text's FIRST appearance in git is 304f24edd at 19:14:24Z, AFTER the skills commit 3e4f50d3a at 19:12:13Z — because agent-father's commit zone excludes docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, so a peer cold-evict swept the board and collapsed the acceptance-write and the lane-move into one indistinguishable blob. The claim is UNVERIFIABLE, not disproven. acceptance_written_by/acceptance_written_at are self-reported fields authored by the same agent whose ordering they attest — they are narration, not evidence.
backlog.po_ruling: The dispatcher's framing is correct and generalises: an agent whose commit zone excludes the board can NEVER produce evidence for an ordering claim about the board. Requiring such a claim therefore mandates an unfalsifiable self-report, which is exactly the failure class feedback_agent_selfreport_metalayer_confabulation.md warns about. The requirement is unenforceable across the whole maintenance lane, and the unsatisfiable dispatch instruction was the dispatcher's error, not agent-father's — no fault attaches to the agent. PREFERRED RESOLUTION: acceptance is authored by the DISPATCHER (or PO) at dispatch time, before spawn. The dispatcher's commit zone already includes the board, so ordering becomes provable by construction across two disjoint zones: dispatcher commits acceptance, implementer commits code, and git ordering across the two zones is independently checkable. Rejected alternatives: (a) letting maintenance agents commit the board row themselves — breaks zone separation and re-introduces the peer-sweep class this very sprint just fixed; (b) silently dropping the requirement — loses the real benefit that acceptance predates implementation.
backlog.question: Should acceptance-criteria authorship move from the implementing agent to the dispatcher for all supervised maintenance-lane rows, and what is the migration path for flow docs that currently instruct the implementer to self-write acceptance?

GENERALIZABLE INVARIANT (make this the AC, not just a tnb patch): a published-marker dedup key period MUST equal the slot cron period. Daily cron -> daily key (published:<slot>:<YYYY-MM-DD>, ttl 100800). Weekly cron -> ISO-week periodKey (ttl 691200). Any slot where these differ silently no-ops for (period/cron - 1) consecutive fires.

Severity P1 (silent no-op on a guaranteed slot), not P0.

SELECTED DESIGN (supersedes options a/b/c in .deliverable — architect may refine the mechanism, NOT re-open the choice): AGED ROUND-ROBIN over the five idle-path consumers, plus DURABLE signal handoff. Two parts, both required; part 2 is NOT optional and NOT separable.

PART 1 — replace the fixed-priority chain with aged round-robin. Today BOUNDED-1 -> SLS -> RLC -> QA-Drain -> Step 1 is a FIXED-PRIORITY chain in which every lane JUMPs to a terminal on dispatch, so the first eligible lane wins every idle tick and the other four are unreachable whenever backlog[] is non-empty (it is: 391). Live evidence says all four non-winners starve, not just Step 1 — so the fix must be lane-generic. One mechanism, four victims.

PART 2 — make the drain->triage handoff DURABLE (folds FIX-DEVTEAM-BOUNDED1-PENDINGSIGNALS-EMPTY-GUARD, now CANCELLED). Rotation alone bounds triage LATENCY but does not stop signal LOSS. Therefore every tick that short-circuits before Step 1 CONSUMES its drained signals and DISCARDS them; recovery is possible only by hand-reading processed/ and only until the 7-day prune. Required: Step 0a persists the drained batch to a durable inbox, Step 1 consumes-and-clears it, so a short-circuited tick loses nothing and the next tick that reaches Step 1 drains the accumulation. backlog.devteam_direction_correction_20260725: DIRECTION CORRECTION (dev-team tick 2026-07-25T13:47Z) — THIS ROW'S STATED MECHANISM IS INVERTED; the fairness fix must not be built on it as written. The title/note assert "with review[] holding qa-eligible rows the QA-Drain fires every idle tick, so PO-bound signal_queue rows accumulate un-triaged", i.e. QA-Drain is named as the PREEMPTOR of Step 1. LIVE GROUND TRUTH 3 days after this row was minted says QA-Drain is the VICTIM, not the preemptor, and has never run at all: (1) grep of the whole hot board for the qa-drain claim stamp `dev-team (review-lane qa-drain)` (scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq line 119) returns ZERO rows; (2) count of rows with status=="QA" in ANY lane is ZERO; (3) meanwhile review[]==109 total with 77 carrying status==REVIEW AND next_agent=="qa" (the exact PRIMARY set that lane claims), up from the 32 review / 10+ qa-eligible this flow doc cites for 2026-07-21; qa[]==0. CAUSE: QA-Drain sits LAST in the head-idle chain (main.md L637, after BOUNDED-1 L496 / SLS L527 / RLC L585) and BOUNDED-1 exits via `JUMP TO execute` (L514) whenever it claims. With backlog[]==389 an eligible unsupervised row is essentially always available, so BOUNDED-1 wins the idle fall-through nearly every tick and control flow never reaches QA-Drain. This is NOT a budget conflict — main.md L645 states QA-Drain has a dedicated `qa[]<1` cap explicitly "NOT the shared WIP<=2 in_progress budget", so the two lanes are designed to run CONCURRENTLY; the starvation is purely the unconditional JUMP, i.e. the same defect class this row already names, but pointing the other way. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: a fairness scheme that merely protects Step 1 PO triage FROM QA-Drain would leave the 77-row review strand permanently frozen, since QA-Drain is upstream-starved by BOUNDED-1 before it can preempt anything. The fix must make the chain fair in BOTH directions (each lane reached on its own independent gate, not gated by an earlier lane's dispatch). backlog.devteam_head_bottleneck_20260725: HEAD-BOTTLENECK (dev-team tick 2026-07-25T13:51Z) — WHY THE INDEPENDENT-BUDGET WORDING CANNOT BE TAKEN AT FACE VALUE, and why simply removing/softening the JUMP will NOT fix this. main.md L645 says QA-Drain has a dedicated `qa[]<1` cap "NOT the shared WIP<=2 in_progress budget", which reads as license for QA-Drain and BOUNDED-1 to run CONCURRENTLY. They cannot, as implemented: all four idle-chain lanes dispatch through the SINGLE `.head` object, and each claim script writes it by FULL REPLACEMENT, not merge — scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq lines 120-131 assign `.head = { status, active_task_id, next_agent, next_action, updated_at, updated_by }` wholesale, same shape as the BOUNDED-1 claim. VERIFIED THIS TICK by inspection before execution: BOUNDED-1 had already claimed FE-PG-QUALITY-AUDIT-LASTVERIFIED-RENDER-FIX and `.head` held {status:in_progress, active_task_id:FE-PG-QUALITY-AUDIT-LASTVERIFIED-RENDER-FIX, next_agent:dev-frontend} with that dev-frontend agent live in the background. Running QA-Drain in the same tick — which its own `qa[]<1` gate WOULD have permitted, qa[]==0 — would have overwritten `.head.active_task_id` to the picked review row and `.head.next_agent` to "qa", severing the in-flight FE task from its head anchor: that task would sit in in_progress[] with no head pointer, and the NEXT tick pipeline-resume (main.md L450) would read the clobbered head and dispatch qa while dev-frontend was still writing files. The QA-Drain run was therefore WITHHELD this tick (not skipped by the JUMP — deliberately withheld after reading the script's write target). IMPLICATION FOR THE FAIRNESS FIX: `.head` is a single-writer dispatch slot, so lane fairness cannot be achieved by reordering the chain or making each lane reachable on its own gate — concurrent lanes would race the same field. The fix needs per-lane dispatch state (e.g. `.head` becomes a map keyed by lane, or each lane tracks its own active_task_id and pipeline-resume iterates them) BEFORE any independent-gate scheme is safe. Until then the chain's sequential JUMP-to-end is load-bearing correctness, not merely a fairness bug — removing it without splitting `.head` would trade starvation for head-clobber corruption.

backlog.title: Session-scoped CronCreate loops are invisible and unpersisted across 5 CLI sessions — build the launchd-hosted liveness watchdog that turns 'a session died and its whole loop vanished' from silent into a BUG-channel alert
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 4 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 (cron-registry.json) landing first; this row is that registry's first consumer. See po_design_ruling below: the design call was made, this row implements one third of it.
backlog.problem: CronList in the router session returns 'No scheduled jobs.' Crons live inside 5 separate CLI sessions (dev-team, cowork, system-audit, claude-heler, workflows-fix). No session can see or repair another's crons. When a session dies its whole loop vanishes with zero trace. CronCreate additionally only fires while the REPL is idle, so a session stuck mid-query fires nothing. PO verified there is NO on-disk cron persistence under ~/.claude (no crons dir; ~/.claude/jobs/ holds two stale June background-job state dirs, unrelated).
backlog.po_design_ruling: OPTION (a) BROADER LAUNCHD COVERAGE — SCOPED, plus (c) MONITORING. Option (b), a persistence/registry layer for CronCreate, is REJECTED as a new scheduler. Reasoning: (1) building persistence for CronCreate means re-implementing a scheduler we do not own, inside a surface (the CLI REPL) whose contract can change under us; we already own two durable planes (launchd, and the containerized mcp-server node-cron scheduler with 85 jobs) and a third home-grown one is exactly the 'duplicating cron hosts' that UC-CDC-P5 already names as the thing to avoid. (2) launchd is the ONLY plane that survives session death and it demonstrably works (firer: 815 runs). (3) But WHOLESALE migration to launchd is equally wrong — `claude -p` per tick is expensive and, per FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION, structurally truncates fan-out work. So launchd hosts loop RE-ARM and LIVENESS, not every loop. (4) The REPL-idle constraint is unfixable from our side; that is a second independent argument for making session-plane failures VISIBLE rather than trying to make the session plane reliable. (5) Monitoring alone (option c as a terminal answer) is also rejected: without a registry there is nothing to monitor against.
backlog.three_part_sequence: PART 1 (registry of record) — FOLDED INTO EXISTING UC-SDF-P6, not re-minted: the 5 session-scoped loops must be DECLARED in a repo file so absence becomes detectable. Not a new scheduler; an inventory. PART 2 (this row) — one launchd-hosted watchdog that reads that registry and alerts when a declared loop has produced no evidence-of-life within its cadence. PART 3 (re-arm automation) — EXISTING UC-CDC-P5, sequenced LAST, only after 1+2: re-arming blind is how you get double-hosted crons.
backlog.hard_constraint_evidence_of_life: Evidence-of-life MUST be the loop's own external artifact — its commits, its notebook mtime, its telemetry row — NEVER a self-report or a heartbeat the loop writes about itself. A loop that can assert its own liveness is a loop whose watchdog is self-satisfying (see FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-FRESHNESS-CHECK-RELOCATE-TO-SENTINEL in ready[], same defect class, already ruled).
backlog.acceptance: Kill any one of the 5 sessions and, within one cadence period, a BUG-channel message names the dead loop. Today that event is completely silent.

backlog.title: Three time bases coexist in one scheduling system: server jobs mix timezone UTC and Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, CronCreate fires at MACHINE-LOCAL France time (CEST/CET, DST-sensitive), and the market it serves is fixed UTC+7 — no single place states what any job's real wall-clock is
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 7 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 cron-registry.json. A registry that records each job's declared time base is most of this answer; doing it before the registry means writing the same table twice.
backlog.problem: (1) mcp-server scheduler jobs individually declare timezone:'UTC' or timezone:'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'. (2) CronCreate jobs fire at machine-local France time (CEST=UTC+2 summer / CET=UTC+1 winter) and therefore SHIFT BY AN HOUR twice a year against the market. (3) Vietnam is fixed UTC+7 with no DST. A job authored as '15:00' has three different meanings depending on which plane it lands on, and nothing declares which.
backlog.dst_is_the_sharp_edge: The France planes silently re-time relative to the VN trading session at each DST transition. docs/standards/cron-jobs.md:292 already documents this reasoning for the guaranteed-slot firer (StartInterval chosen over StartCalendarInterval precisely because the latter is DST-sensitive) — the insight exists but is applied in exactly one place. Next transitions to check against: late Oct 2026 (CEST->CET) shifts every session-plane cron one hour LATER relative to UTC/VN.
backlog.folded_item_5b_minute_collision: FOLDED (item 5b, LOW): restartCadenceAlert (server plane) and cron-db-data-integrity (terminal/session plane) both sit on `15,45 * * * *`. PO assessment: these run in different processes and share no resource except SQLite, so this is a same-minute COINCIDENCE, not a contention bug — it is folded here rather than minted separately because a cron-registry with declared time bases is what makes cross-plane minute maps computable at all, instead of discoverable only by hand-audit.
backlog.explicitly_out_of_scope_verified_good: The auditor :00/:30 vs dev-team :07/:37 vs db-integrity :15/:45 offsets are CORRECT and deliberate. Do NOT 'fix', 'normalize' or 'align' them. Any change that collapses those offsets is a regression.

Systemd default StartLimitIntervalSec=10s/StartLimitBurst=5 causes permanent failed state for any Restart=always unit crashing >=5 times in 10s window. Hardening has been proven safe by commit 42e8448ce (applied to vn-news-fetch/vn-reuters-fetch/vn-tradingeconomics-fetch 2026-05-02) — vn-news-fetch rode through the same incident window unaffected, demonstrating the control. This incident was non-recoverable without manual intervention due to inbound SSH/HTTP being blocked to VPS (user-gated restart already escalated via Telegram).

backlog.title: PUBLISHED-MARKER KEY AGREEMENT — derive the dedup key from the scheduled UTC fire-window, never from a wall-clock date read (P0: chef-evening double-published 2026-07-22 19:56Z + 20:00Z on keys :2026-07-22 vs :2026-07-23 derived from ONE instant; the same defect will FALSELY SUPPRESS the 2026-07-23 19:45Z dish)
backlog.note:
ROOT CAUSE (RAW-verified 2026-07-22T20:00-20:10Z, router + po). chef-evening cron is `45 19 * * *` = 19:45 UTC = 02:45 VN of D+1 — cowork-schedule.json chef-evening.vn_description literally reads '02:45 VN next day (GMT+7)'. chef.md Step 0.5 L48 computes WORK_DATE = TZ="Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh" date +%Y-%m-%d and L70 builds MARKER_KEY = published:<slot>:<WORK_DATE>. Because this slot fires AFTER VN midnight, the key straddles a date boundary: two peers reading the SAME wall-clock instant derive DIFFERENT keys. EVIDENCE — task_list_held(task_kind=cowork-slot) shows BOTH published:chef-evening:2026-07-22 (owner_client_session 9f4a6bfc-b001-4349-8a44-545f24c1b0ac, claimed_at 1784750141 = 19:55:41Z) AND published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 (owner_client_session ab870ed6-0502-4e49-811a-8e7c90aff1ef, claimed_at 1784750490 = 20:01:30Z) HELD SIMULTANEOUSLY, ttl_seconds 100800 each. Both runs therefore claimed successfully, both passed the gate, both published. Artifacts on disk, both dish_type=evening + quality_verdict=degraded, overlapping conviction VHM+VIC: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-22-evening.json (date_vn 2026-07-22, timestamp_utc 19:56:15Z, EIB/VIC/VHM/VJC, regime risk-off) and docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-23-evening.json (date_vn 2026-07-23, timestamp_utc 20:00:37Z, VHM/VIC/VCB, regime carry-unwind-risk-off). NOTE the historical convention was the UTC/trading-day label — published:chef-evening:2026-07-21 was claimed 2026-07-21T19:51:10Z i.e. VN 07-22 — so the 19:55Z run followed PRECEDENT while the 20:01Z run followed the SPEC AS WRITTEN. Neither agent misbehaved. The spec is ambiguous exactly at the boundary it is supposed to defend.

WHY THIS IS **NOT** UC-CCA-P3 — DO NOT FOLD AND CLOSE. UC-CCA-P3 fixes marker LIFECYCLE (claim timing + release immunity). Its design recommendation (early read-only probe + late task_claim immediately before send_telegram + never release) would NOT have prevented this incident: both peers would still compute DIFFERENT keys, both probes would read free, both late claims would succeed, both would publish. Key AGREEMENT is orthogonal to key LIFECYCLE. A mutex whose key depends on which timezone the reader happens to consult is not a mutex. If UC-CCA-P3 ships alone, this defect survives and the umbrella closes green — the recurring-detection-vs-recurring-FAILED-FIX class (feedback_recurring_detection_vs_recurring_failed_fix).

PO RULING (product decision, po-owned, decided 2026-07-22 — DO NOT re-litigate; architect/ba own the HOW, not the WHAT). The dedup key and the human-readable date label are TWO DIFFERENT VALUES and MUST NOT be derived from one expression. chef.md L654 (CYCLE_DATE = WORK_DATE verbatim) deliberately couples them; that coupling IS the defect, not the fix — it was introduced by GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A-FLOW-PERSIST to make the FILENAME deterministic and it silently made the MUTEX KEY timezone-dependent. (1) MUTEX KEY = window-anchored and timezone-free: derived from the scheduled cron fire-window expressed in UTC (shape e.g. published:<slot_id>:2026-07-22T19:45Z), NOT from any `date` call made by the executing agent. Two peers executing the same scheduled window MUST derive byte-identical keys with zero shared state beyond the cron expression. This is invariant to timezone, to VN/UTC midnight straddle, to DST, to host clock skew, and to run-start jitter within the window (19:55 vs 20:01). It needs NO trading-calendar lookup. NEVER put a trading-calendar / holiday lookup on the mutex path. (2) DISPLAY LABEL (metadata.date_vn, synthesis filename, prose) = the VN trading session the dish INFORMS. chef-evening fires after the prior VN close (08:00Z) and before the next VN open (02:00Z of D+1) and gates on macroIndicatorRefreshJob US macro data — it is a FORWARD preview; the slot's own dish_type is literally `evening_preview`. Therefore the correct label for a 19:45Z fire is the NEXT VN session = the VN wall date at fire time. Tonight's correct label is 2026-07-23; the 19:55Z run's date_vn=2026-07-22 is WRONG. Weekend/holiday note for ba: the cron is daily including weekends, so 'next VN session' is not the next calendar day on Fri/Sat/Sun fires — the LABEL MAY remain the plain VN wall date (simple, calendar-free); if a true session label is ever wanted it belongs in a SEPARATE display-only field and never in the key.

CAUTION for architect/ba: metadata.cycle_id is NOT a ready-made substitute — today's two runs emitted cycle_id evening-2026-07-22T19:56:00Z and evening-2026-07-22T20:00:37Z, i.e. cycle_id is keyed to RUN-START and diverges exactly like WORK_DATE does. RECOMMENDED PLUMBING (non-binding): the cowork dispatcher ALREADY holds the canonical window value — the fire-election lock cron:cowork:2026-07-22T20:00Z carries payload.tick — so pass the tick DOWN to the spawned agent instead of having the agent re-derive it; DESIGN-COWORK-FANOUT-T1-TICK-SNAPSHOT-WON-SLOTS (tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7, already in ready[]) is the natural carrier. Deriving-at-the-leaf is what created this bug class.

LIVE FORWARD HAZARD (self-healing — do NOT 'fix' it with lock surgery): published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 expires 2026-07-24T00:01:30Z, which is AFTER tomorrow's 2026-07-23T19:45Z fire. If tomorrow's run uses the UTC-date convention it derives :2026-07-23, finds it HELD, and SILENTLY SKIPS — a MISSED evening dish. If it uses the VN convention it derives :2026-07-24 and publishes. Tomorrow's outcome is a coin flip on which convention the spawned agent picks. So this ONE defect produces BOTH double-publish AND missed-publish. Both markers are deliberately LEFT IN PLACE: they are the evidence, and releasing published: markers is the known-wrong direction (feedback_chef_releases_published_marker_enables_peer_double_publish). Hazard self-clears 2026-07-24T00:01:30Z.

AC: (1) two peers spawned for the SAME scheduled window derive byte-identical MARKER_KEY regardless of host timezone, of VN-vs-UTC midnight straddle, and of run-start offset within the window; (2) the key contains NO value obtained from a `date` call made by the executing agent; (3) mutex key and display label are SEPARATE named values with separate derivations, and no later step re-derives either; (4) chef-evening's synthesis date_vn + filename carry the NEXT-VN-session label per the PO ruling above; (5) the fix applies to ALL cowork published: gates (chef-morning/intraday/eod/evening, digest-daily, digest-sunday, fb, market-watcher, news-scout, tnb-audit) — not chef-evening alone; the same straddle hits ANY slot whose UTC fire hour maps across VN midnight, and single-fire slots carry a 100800s TTL that outlives the next window; (6) RAW-verify by executing two same-window runs: exactly ONE claim succeeds, exactly ONE synthesis artifact exists for the window, exactly ONE MARKET post is emitted.

SEQUENCING: ships WITH UC-CCA-P3, not before and not after — lifecycle-without-key-agreement is defeated by divergent keys, key-agreement-without-lifecycle is defeated by leaked or released markers. architect should treat UC-CCA-P3 + this row as ONE design.

RECURRENCE LEDGER (marker-gate cluster): 2026-07-02 x2 (chef-morning + chef-evening, release-after-publish), 07-03 (release-on-no-post remediation -> leak-on-silent-exit), 07-14 (chef-evening dup + date mislabel), 07-15 (MARKET ids 932+933; the dup published a FALSE ~29% index move), 07-16 (chef-eod abort-after-claim false tombstone), 07-17 (chef-eod 2nd false tombstone), 07-22 (THIS — key divergence, NEW root cause). 8th event, 3rd distinct root cause. Recurring-bug-escalation applies (feedback_recurring_bug_escalation): no further point-patches to Step 0.5 until this + UC-CCA-P3 land as one design.

backlog.title: cowork-team parallel fan-out has no producer/consumer ordering — alert-commander read the signal bus before its co-dispatched producers wrote to it, and went silent on a session with real >5% drops
backlog.mechanism: BGFAN-1 mandates run_in_background=true for every dispatcher spawn and spawn-fanout.md issues all matched slots in ONE parallel block, with no dependency ordering. When a tick matches both a PRODUCER (market-watcher -> price_anomaly; news-scout -> urgent_news/chain_catalyst) and a CONSUMER (alert-commander -> gates on those exact signal types), the consumer can complete its bus read before the producers have posted.

backlog.detail: SPIKE item #1 — the HIGH-severity follow-up that was dropped when items #2/#3/#4 were minted 2026-07-10 (FIX-CYCLEJOB-1294-FOLLOWUP-SWEEP, FIX-RAG-TEMPORAL-DECAY-TEST-JITTER, CI-PERFILE-STRUCTURAL-MITIGATION all exist; this one never got a row). Root cause of the recurring CI RED on 1299b-skill-gated-bootstrap.test.ts, re-observed this tick: CI run 29464553988 @ head 571818c2d = 14498 pass / 1 fail, delta since last GREEN 25cb69031 is 4 docs/chore/orch-state commits with ZERO product code; local isolated repro 9/9 pass 549ms. Mechanism: agentBootstrap.ts:358 `const toolNameMap = buildToolNameMap()` eagerly + synchronously probes ~107 tool-registration fns at module top-level; registerAgentMemoryTools -> getProjectRoot() runs blocking execSync('git rev-parse --show-toplevel') (projectRoot.ts:16). Under CPU starvation the git fork stalls past bun's 5s per-test timeout; the mid-flight-errored ES module instance is then permanently TDZ-poisoned ('Cannot access toolNameMap before initialization'), cascading to every remaining test in the file (6/9 failed in worst reproduced run, 11/24 runs under contention per SPIKE). Also a genuine production cold-start latency risk: server.ts:40 imports agentBootstrap on the live MCP boot path and ~30 test files import it transitively (this is the 'rotating failing file' blast radius). FIX options: remove the subprocess from the eval path -> memoize project-root via import.meta.dir walk-up (no git spawn), OR make registerAgentMemoryTools' project-root resolution lazy (resolve at tool-invocation, not at the registration probe). AC: no execSync on the module-eval path + cold-start non-regression guard + all ~107 tool names resolve + 1299b 9/9 green + ~30 agentBootstrap-importer tests green. PLAN-ONLY backlog for BOUNDED-1 — do NOT dispatch this tick.

backlog.title: system-auditor C-04 counts bulk-reparse re-stamps as new low-confidence extractions (parsed_at is a mutation timestamp, not arrival) AND counts never-extracted rows (conf=0, status=pending) as low-confidence -> recurring WARN false-positive
backlog.root_cause: C-04 (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:572) = SELECT count(*) FROM financial_reports WHERE parsed_at > datetime('now','-7 days') AND extraction_confidence < 0.2, threshold <=5. TWO independent predicate defects, both RAW-probed by PO against live market.db in the mcp-server runtime. D1 RECENCY: parsed_at is a MUTATION timestamp bumped by any reparse, not an arrival timestamp. All 11 flagged rows have parsed_at in {2026-07-19, 2026-07-20} and NONE since; that 2-day window parsed 182 rows total against a historical baseline of 1-23 rows/WEEK — i.e. a bulk historical reparse batch re-stamped a legacy cohort into the 7-day window. Periods flagged are 2024-Q1..2025-Q4, not current filings. The 11 are 6.0% of the 182-row batch — a HEALTHY rate, not an extractor regression. D2 POPULATION: extraction_confidence < 0.2 sweeps in rows that were never extracted at all — 5 of the 11 (HUT 2024-Q1, HUT 2024-Q3, HUT 2025-Q3, BSR 2024-Q3, HUT 2025-Q4) — leaving only 6 rows that are genuinely low_confidence — carry conf=0.0 with validation_status in {pending, pending_extraction}. 'Not yet extracted' is not 'low-confidence extraction'; 45% of the alert population is mislabelled. An absolute count threshold (<=5) with no volume normalisation guarantees re-fire on every future bulk reparse.
backlog.deliverable: Re-specify C-04: (a) normalise to a RATE with a minimum-volume floor (e.g. lowconf/total > 15% AND total >= 20) instead of an absolute count, so healthy large batches do not trip it; (b) restrict the population to rows that actually completed extraction — exclude validation_status in ('pending','pending_extraction') and/or require extraction_confidence IS NOT NULL AND > 0; (c) decide whether recency should key off an immutable arrival column (published_at) rather than parsed_at, or whether the reparse path should stop re-stamping parsed_at. Fold into scripts/auditor-db-checks.sh as predicate SSOT per UC-ASL-P3 rather than leaving raw SQL in the flow doc.
backlog.acceptance: Replaying the live 2026-07-19/20 reparse batch through the new predicate emits ZERO C-04 signal. Negative control: a synthetic cohort where >15% of a >=20-row genuinely-extracted batch lands under 0.2 confidence STILL trips C-04. No never-extracted (pending*) row appears in the counted population.

backlog.title: Add a real updated_at audit column to prediction_claims, maintained on every write, surfaced per-row on the Du bao AI page so a reader can tell at a glance whether a prediction was actually refreshed
backlog.root_cause: Direct user demand: 'each prediction need add update at time for easy recheck is update or not'. VERIFIED ABSENT end-to-end. The store row type PredictionClaimRow (predictionClaimStore.ts:60, mapRow ~:110) exposes exactly: id, stock, agent_id, claim_text, direction, target_price, resolution_date, confidence, resolution_outcome, actual_price, brier_score, creation_price, is_excluded, created_at, resolved_at — no updated_at. The serve DTO (predictionClaimsHandler.ts) and the page type (dashboard.prediction-claims.tsx:82-83) carry only createdAt and resolvedAt. PO DECISION — ADD A REAL COLUMN, do not repurpose an existing timestamp. Reasoning: (1) resolvedAt is the closest existing candidate but it is NULL for all 5 pending rows in live data, which is exactly the population the user wants to recheck — surfacing it would answer 'was this updated?' with a blank for every row the question is actually about; (2) createdAt answers a different question (when minted) and by construction never moves; (3) FIX-PREDCLAIM-CREATIONPRICE-UNGATE-ZOD-CONTRACT deliverable (c) and FIX-PREDCLAIM-BACKFILL-NULL-CREATIONPRICE both introduce a genuine THIRD mutation class — post-creation edits to a claim that are neither creation nor resolution — after which no existing timestamp can represent 'last touched' at all; (4) the backfill will rewrite historical rows, and without an audit column there is no way for a reader to distinguish a backfilled row from an untouched one, which is precisely the recheck affordance being asked for.
backlog.deliverable: (a) mcp-server: add updated_at to prediction_claims using the ESTABLISHED idempotent pattern already in schema-system.ts:209-212 (try { db.exec('ALTER TABLE prediction_claims ADD COLUMN updated_at TEXT') } catch {}) — same shape as the creation_price and is_excluded columns added before it. Do not introduce a new migration mechanism for one column. (b) Maintain it on EVERY write path with no exceptions: insertPredictionClaim sets updated_at = created_at; resolveClaim and excludeClaim set it to now; the backfill script sets it; any future partial-update helper sets it. Stamping must live inside the store functions, not at call sites — a call-site convention is exactly the kind of thing the next new call site skips. Use real UTC from the runtime, never a hand-formed string (feedback_hand_typed_iso_timestamps_drift_into_the_future.md). (c) Backfill existing rows: updated_at = COALESCE(resolved_at, created_at), which is truthful for every row under the current two-event lifecycle. (d) Extend the serve DTO in predictionClaimsHandler.ts with updatedAt, passing through as null where genuinely unset — never coerced, matching the existing 'all nullable columns pass through as null' rule in mapClaimRow. (e) frontend: render it per claim on dashboard.prediction-claims.tsx as 'Cap nhat luc', clearly distinct from the creation date, and legible for pending rows. (f) Fold updated_at into the Zod contract from FIX-PREDCLAIM-CREATIONPRICE-UNGATE-ZOD-CONTRACT as a REQUIRED field on write once the column exists.
backlog.acceptance: Every one of the 17 live claims returns a non-null updatedAt through the LIVE served endpoint after backfill. A claim mutated by the backfill script shows an updatedAt strictly later than its createdAt; an untouched historical claim shows updatedAt equal to its resolved_at or created_at. Resolving a pending claim advances its updatedAt within the same tick. The value is visible per row on the rendered page. All timestamps are runtime-generated UTC — no hand-typed ISO strings anywhere in the change.
backlog.note: zone=multi because the change spans apps/mcp-server/ (column + store stamping + DTO) and apps/frontend/ (render) — architect splits per the precedent set by FIX-PRED-CLAIMS-EXCLUDED-SERVE-DISPLAY, which was minted zone=multi (commit c40f90062) and dispatched to dev-mcp-server + dev-frontend in parallel (commit b0a786690). Sequenced P2 behind the three P1 rows: an updated_at on a claim that is still structurally unscoreable would tell the user when a worthless row was last touched. Fix the scoring first, then give the reader the recheck affordance.

backlog.title: A-30 clause-4 ADDITIONAL VETO predicate `vmhwm_kb > vmrss_kb` is a tautology, not a discriminator — VmHWM is a monotone high-water mark so the test is true for any process not sitting exactly at its lifetime peak; it downgrades EVERY ESCALATE to PASS (including the OOMKilled CRITICAL branch, which it pre-empts by ordering) and converted a real sustained-95-96%-no-reclamation finding into `0 anomalies` on the 2026-07-25 12:30Z Tier-1 tick
backlog.root_cause: docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:167-171, clause 4 of the A-30 Memory Reclamation Discriminator block shipped by FIX-AUDITOR-A12A20A30-FP-REEMIT-CONVERGE (2026-07-23, DONE, commit 2f956f1c5): 'if verdict=="ESCALATE" AND vmhwm_kb and vmrss_kb are both numeric AND vmhwm_kb > vmrss_kb -> downgrade to PASS, no emit'. DEFECT 1 — TAUTOLOGY: VmHWM is /proc/<pid>/status's peak-resident-set high-water mark and is monotonically non-decreasing over process lifetime; VmRSS is instantaneous. Therefore VmHWM >= VmRSS holds by construction, and VmHWM > VmRSS is FALSE only in the knife-edge instant where current RSS equals the all-time peak. The predicate carries approximately zero information about memory safety: it answers 'has this process ever freed a page', never 'where does the peak sit relative to the cap'. Three router-captured samples on the SAME mcp-server container 2026-07-25, all three vetoing identically: 12:38Z (auditor's own pre-swap sample) VmHWM 2851248kB / VmRSS 2841768kB, ~93% of the 3GiB cap -> VmHWM>VmRSS TRUE -> PASS; 12:42:26Z (router, pre-swap) VmHWM 3084864kB = 98.1% OF CAP / VmRSS 2949772kB = 93.28% -> TRUE -> PASS; 12:47:46Z (router, post-swap 3-minute-old container) VmHWM 327700kB = 10.4% of cap / VmRSS 311208kB = 10.79% -> TRUE -> would PASS. Identical verdict at 98.1% of cap and at 10.4% of cap. DEFECT 1b — SIGN IS ARGUABLY INVERTED near the cap: a WIDER VmHWM-minus-VmRSS gap on a process close to its limit simultaneously proves the process has already touched an even higher fraction of the cap (12:42:26Z: the very reading the clause reads as reassurance is the reading that shows a 98.1%-of-cap peak). DEFECT 2 — PRECEDENCE: clause 4 is written to run BEFORE clause 5's verdict/reason mapping, so it pre-empts ALL of clause 5, including `verdict==ESCALATE` + reason `OOMKilled=true` -> CRITICAL and `peak >97%` -> CRITICAL. A container that was genuinely OOM-killed and restarted presents a fresh process whose VmHWM > VmRSS almost immediately, so the confirmed-OOM CRITICAL branch is reachable in practice only when VM data is UNAVAILABLE. Upstream script is NOT at fault and was deliberately left unmodified by the converge row: scripts/audits/verify-a30-mcp-memory-reclamation.sh:93-97 computes three already-discriminating ESCALATE conditions (OOMKilled=true; reclamation_dips==0 AND min_pct>93; reclamation_dips==0 AND max_pct>97) plus an intra-window reclamation-DEPTH signal (`dips` = consecutive-sample downward step >0.5pp, :83) that the veto layer discards. DEMONSTRATED CONSEQUENCE 2026-07-25 12:30Z Tier-1 tick: the auditor ran the deep probe as instructed, obtained raw verdict=ESCALATE (samples sustained 95-96%, zero reclamation dips in ANY sample -> the min_pct>93 branch), applied clause 4, and returned 'DONE: Audit complete tier-1 — 0 anomalies (0 critical, 0 warn, 0 info)' with '[OUTPUT-CONTRACT] signals_posted=0 | telegram_sent=0 | signal_queue_rows_written=0 | dashboard_rows=0'. The agent behaved CORRECTLY — the flow told it to veto. PO corroborated BY ABSENCE, not by the agent's assertion (re-verified 2026-07-25T12:50Z): signal_queue.rows still 125 / archive 0; docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md still 186L; `git log --since=12:00Z` shows zero system-auditor commits. backlog.title: sla-monitor's bctc threshold is NOT a policy constant — it rises 60min/hour in lockstep with the measured staleness, holding a fixed 5439-minute margin. The gate can therefore never clear and never escalates, and the 'threshold' value printed in every CRITICAL alert is meaningless.
backlog.status_note:
MECHANICALLY PROVEN, not inferred. PO extracted every bctc sla-monitor alert from list_unresolved_reports() over a 21-hour window (2026-07-24T17:00Z -> 2026-07-25T14:00Z, 12 samples) and differenced the two numbers in each message:
  stale=5950 thr=511 | 6010/571 | 6070/631 | 6160/721 | 6250/811 | 6340/901 | 6400/961 | 6550/1111 | 6700/1261 | 6910/1471 | 7090/1651 | 7210/1771
The set of (stale - threshold) values across all 12 samples is EXACTLY {5439}. One element. The threshold is not a duration policy — it is a second clock running 5439 minutes behind the first.

ISOLATED TO bctc, WHICH IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL THAT MAKES THIS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A GLOBAL MISREADING: in the same alert stream over the same window, every other metric's threshold is CONSTANT — bond_maturity 10080 (7d) in all samples, signal_quality_audit 2880 (48h) in all, news 30, sbv_fx 30. Only the bctc threshold moves. So this is a bctc-specific threshold computation, not a shared formatter bug and not an artifact of how the message is rendered.

HYPOTHESIS FOR THE ROOT CAUSE, stated as a hypothesis and NOT verified at source (PO did not read the sla-monitor implementation — the next agent must): a constant difference between two quantities that both grow with wall-clock time means BOTH are ages measured from `now` against FIXED timestamps, 5439 minutes apart. That is, the code is almost certainly comparing `now - T_data` against `now - T_other` — an AGE-vs-AGE comparison — where a correct SLA compares an AGE against a DURATION. Whoever picks this up should first confirm or refute that shape before changing anything; if it is refuted, the 5439 constant still has to be explained.

OPERATIONAL COST: the bctc breach re-fires roughly hourly and has done so continuously for at least 21 hours (almost certainly far longer — 3 samples/hour of bond_maturity + signal_quality_audit + bctc dominate the 100-row unresolved-report backlog). Because the margin is fixed, the alert carries zero information about whether the situation is improving or worsening: it will print CRITICAL with a larger pair of numbers forever.

That fixes the NUMERATOR (population). This row fixes the COMPARATOR. Both can be true at once and fixing either alone leaves the alert wrong.

MINTED 2026-07-25T16:31:11Z by po. Split out of the context_bloat_breach triage because NO PRUNER FIX CAN REACH THIS FILE — verified at source, not inferred.

docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md is 120183 bytes (10x the 12000-byte cap) across 190 lines, and it contains EXACTLY ONE "## " section, titled "## This session", which alone accounts for 119035 of those bytes. Measured this tick.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE ROW FROM FIX-NOTEBOOK-PRUNER-LINE-ONLY-SETPOINT-BYTE-CAP-NEVER-CONVERGES. That row corrects scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh to stop at bytes as well as lines, which self-heals every correctly-sectioned notebook on its next write. It cannot help this file under EITHER axis, for two independent reasons: (1) at 190 lines the file is UNDER the 200-line cap, so the pruner early-exits at :135 without ever inspecting it; (2) even once a byte setpoint makes it eligible, the pruner's only mechanism is to drop the OLDEST "## " section, and with a single section there is nothing to drop — it falls straight to the safe-fail branch at :179, emits notebook_single_section_overage_breach, and deliberately does not truncate. This file is structurally immune to the class fix. A reader who sees the pruner row land and assumes alert-commander is covered will be wrong.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS A WRITE-DISCIPLINE VIOLATION, NOT A SIZE PROBLEM. .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md:83 lists alert-commander in the APPEND class, whose contract is per-cycle "## " sections subject to AC-2 retention, AC-2b intra-prune and the ~60L-per-section rule. Sibling APPEND-class notebooks honour it — news-scout carries 24 sections ("## c200 · 2026-07-25T16:14:39Z ..."), qa 21, main 16, tran-ngoc-bau 5. alert-commander instead maintains a single perpetually-growing "## This session" blob, so the retention machinery the whole scheme depends on has nothing to grip. It is not writing slightly too much; it is not writing in the required shape at all, and has not been for long enough to accumulate 119KB.

CORROBORATION THAT THIS IS THE WORST OFFENDER AND IS ACTIVELY WORSENING: 24 of the 87 processed context-bloat breach signals in docs/signals/processed/ name this file — more than any other, spanning 2026-07-23T16:13Z to 2026-07-25T16:15Z, roughly one every two hours for 48 hours. The file grew 182->190 lines during the very session that relayed the breach. Every one of those 24 signals was filed as processed with the condition untouched.

REMEDY — TWO PARTS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT LASTS.
  1. STRUCTURAL (the durable fix, this row's core): bring alert-commander's notebook write onto the APPEND-class contract — per-cycle "## c<N> · <ISO-8601>" sections so AC-2 retention and the corrected byte-aware pruner can both operate. Locate the agent's notebook-write step in docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/ and repoint it at the notebook-write skill rather than whatever bespoke single-section append it performs today. po did NOT read the alert-commander flow files this tick and is NOT asserting where the deviation lives — find it before changing anything, and if the flow already routes through the skill correctly then the defect is in execution rather than instruction and the finding must be re-scoped, not forced.

ONE-OFF REMEDIATION: the existing 119KB blob must be split into dated sections or archived to docs/agent-memory/notebooks/archive/ (the archive path is line-cap EXEMPT per the T1 case in context-bloat-backstop.test.sh, so it is the sanctioned destination) before the pruner can maintain it. Do the structural fix FIRST — remediating the file while the write discipline is unchanged just restarts the 48-hour clock, which is exactly the trap that produced 24 identical signals.

INTERIM RELIEF IS ALREADY ROUTED AND IS NOT THIS ROW: the two live context_bloat_breach signals name claude-manager-helper as owner, and a manual prune by that agent is legitimate immediate relief. It is symptomatic — it does not close this row, and this row must not be marked done on the strength of a prune.
