backlog.title: orch-state `blocks` AND `co_edit` are write-only — read by NO script, so any sequencing or atomic-ship guard expressed in them is decorative. PO authored one of each on 2026-07-25 believing both bound; neither did. 7 rows carry `blocks` (1 holds a prose paragraph instead of task ids), 2 rows carry `co_edit`
backlog.source: dev-team 16:37Z tick caught PO's own decorative guard on FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES; mechanism + full-repo reader grep + 7-row population + positive control independently re-verified at source by po
backlog.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T17:00:10Z by po. Surfaced by the dev-team 16:37Z tick, which caught PO's own decorative guard; independently re-verified at source by po before minting. The reporter explicitly declined to mint and left the call to PO.

THE DEFECT. `blocks` reads as a sequencing constraint and binds NOTHING. It is write-only across the entire repo. An author who writes `blocks: ["X"]` on row A, intending "X must not start before A", has created zero enforcement — and, critically, has no way to tell the difference from a working gate by inspecting the board.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, NOT RELAYED:
  - scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:133-141 — `effective_depends_on` unions ONLY the candidate row's own `.depends_on`, `.depends` and `.blocked_by`; inline first, then backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows. It never traverses a reverse edge from any other row.
  - :161-164 — `deps_satisfied` short-circuits `true` when the effective list is empty.
  - Full grep across scripts/lib/*.jq, scripts/devteam-*.jq, scripts/orch-*.mjs, scripts/orch-*.sh, scripts/agents-flow/*.sh: NO consumer of `blocks`. The only textual matches are unrelated test-assertion prose ("... blocks idle").

LIVE POPULATION — 7 rows carry the field, and the three states are instructive:
  - INERT-BUT-INTENDED (1): FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT -> FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES. This was PO's own guard, written 16:49Z today, believed binding, and it was not. Now repaired by writing the reciprocal `depends_on` inline on the target. THIS IS THE PROOF THE FIELD IS A TRAP: a caller whose entire job is board correctness used it wrongly on the same day, because nothing about it signals that it does not work.
  - ACCIDENTALLY-BINDING (1): RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND -> ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-REBUILD-CRON. This one DOES hold — but not because of the `blocks` edge. The target independently carries `blocked_by: ["ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-CRON-SAFETY-GATE", "RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND"]` and status BLOCKED. Positive control for the correct shape, and evidence that the correct shape is already known and used elsewhere in the same board. Verified at source rather than assumed.
  - MALFORMED (1): FIX-MCP-SUITE-HEALTH-BASELINE's `blocks` value is not a task id or a list of them — it is a prose paragraph beginning "PUSH-AUTONOMY-1. This standing red makes any literal '0 fail on the FULL suite' reading of the push gate permanently unsatisfiable...". A separate data-quality defect that only survives because nothing ever parses the field. It is IN SCOPE for this row: whichever remedy is chosen must not silently swallow a non-list value.
  - EMPTY / harmless (4): TASK_2006, TASK_2005, ALPHA-S2-SUB5-WATCHDOG-STRETCH, ALPHA-S2-FF-SUB6-BUCKETING-HELPER all carry `blocks: []`.

REMEDY — THREE HONEST OPTIONS, po did NOT choose:
  [a] MAKE THE GATE READ THE REVERSE EDGE — extend `effective_depends_on` to also scan every lane for rows whose `blocks` contains the candidate's id. Most faithful to author intent, and fixes all existing writers retroactively. Costs a full-board scan per candidate inside a hot eligibility predicate; measure before adopting.
  [b] MAKE `blocks` AN ALIAS — have scripts/orch-apply.sh mirror `A.blocks: [X]` into `X.blocked_by += [A]` at write time, so the reverse edge is normalised into the forward field the gates already read. Keeps the eligibility predicate untouched and cheap. Needs care: mirroring must be idempotent, must not fight a hand-written `blocked_by`, and must fail loud on a non-list value (see the malformed row above) rather than mirroring garbage.
  [c] DELETE THE FIELD — strip `blocks` from all 7 rows and forbid it, forcing every sequencing intent through `depends_on`/`blocked_by`. Smallest surface, but discards genuinely useful documentation-of-intent and does nothing to stop the next author reaching for an intuitive name.
WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE is leaving a field that reads as a constraint in every board dump while binding nothing. If [c] is chosen, the deletion must be paired with something that makes the mistake loud — see acceptance 3.

SCOPE ITEM DISCOVERED WHILE REPAIRING THE INSTANCE — A SECOND WAY DEP GATES CAN SILENTLY OPEN. scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh defaults `STUB_FIELDS="id,title,priority,size,type,zone,status,sprint,detail_ref"`. `depends_on`, `depends` and `blocked_by` are NOT in the keep-set, so a re-run strips inline deps out of hot rows. That is normally survivable because `effective_depends_on` falls back to backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows — BUT the strip is documented idempotent with "existing cold wins" (docs/policies/dev-standards.md), so a row whose cold entry already carries `depends_on: null` (as FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES does today) would lose the inline value while the stale cold null survives. Net effect: a dependency that was set correctly, later silently unset by an unrelated maintenance migration. Either add the three dep field names to STUB_FIELDS, or make the cold-merge non-clobbering for dep fields specifically. This belongs here because it is the same failure mode by a different route: a gate that is present in the author's mental model and absent from the machine's.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. A sequencing intent expressed the way PO expressed it at 16:49Z (reverse `blocks` edge only, target row otherwise unconstrained) either BINDS or is REJECTED AT WRITE TIME. It must not be silently accepted and ignored.
  2. The existing 7 `blocks`-carrying rows are each dispositioned — migrated, normalised, or deleted — with the malformed FIX-MCP-SUITE-HEALTH-BASELINE prose value handled explicitly rather than crashing or being swallowed.
  3. NEGATIVE CONTROL, and this is the criterion that distinguishes a real fix from a cleanup: after the change, deliberately author a new reverse-only `blocks` guard and demonstrate that it is caught — by binding, by a validation error, or by a loud warning. A remedy that only fixes today's 7 rows leaves the trap armed for the next author.
  4. STUB_FIELDS (or the cold-merge rule) preserves `depends_on`/`depends`/`blocked_by`, verified by running the stub migration over a fixture row carrying an inline dep and asserting the dep still binds afterwards.
  5. Do NOT hand-edit docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json as part of this — 761KB, outside the orch-apply validation gate.

CROSS-REF, NOT A NEW INSTANCE: this is adjacent to SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP (ready/P1) but deliberately NOT filed as an instance there. That row's class is gates whose INPUT cannot cross a threshold; here there is no gate at all — the field simply has no consumer. Filing it there would dilute a class that row has carefully bounded. The transferable lesson does belong in that SPIKE's findings doc as one line, however: A FIELD'S EXISTENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A CONSUMER — when auditing any guard expressed as data, grep for its READER before trusting it.

The STUB_FIELDS residual is IN SCOPE for this row and the cheap remedy is ENDORSED: add depends_on, depends and blocked_by to the STUB_FIELDS default at scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh:57 (currently id,title,priority,size,type,zone,status,sprint,detail_ref). Independently re-verified: the script contains ZERO occurrences of any dep field name, and combined with its documented existing-cold-wins merge, a re-run would strip an inline dep from a hot row while a stale cold null survives — silently re-opening a gate that was set correctly. One line, no cold-file surgery. EXPLICITLY REJECTED as the remedy here: hand-editing docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json (761KB, outside the orch-apply validation gate) — the cure is worse than the risk, and it would fix one row rather than the class. ACCEPTANCE ADDITION (this row's AC 4 already names it, restated concretely): run the stub migration over a fixture row carrying an inline depends_on and assert, by EXECUTING scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq deps_satisfied rather than by reading the field, that the dep still binds afterwards.
backlog.po_coedit_foldin_20260725T1737:
po 2026-07-25T17:37Z — SECOND INSTANCE FOLDED IN: `co_edit`. NO NEW ROW MINTED (grep-for-prior-art ruling; the reporter recommended folding and po agrees — this row's scope and its AC 3 negative control extend to it without modification).

THE INSTANCE. On 2026-07-25 at ~17:2xZ po wrote a `co_edit` binding onto BOTH Step 0b sibling rows (FIX-DEVTEAM-BACKGROUND-SPAWN-LOCK-RELEASED-AT-SPAWN-NOT-COMPLETION and FIX-DEVTEAM-STEP0B-RESUME-SUPERVISED-HOLD-GATE), intending "these two must be edited in ONE change to the Step 0b block, because shipping them separately means the second edit races the first." It binds nothing.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY po THIS TICK, WITH A WIDER NET THAN THE REPORT USED. The report grepped `scripts/ apps/` for .jq/.js/.sh/.ts and got 0 files. po re-ran it across the ENTIRE repo with no path or extension restriction (`grep -rl "co_edit" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .`) — 3 files total, and every one of them is a WRITER or a record of a write, never a reader:
  docs/data/orch/orch-state.json      (the 2 rows carrying the field, + this note)
  docs/agent-memory/notebooks/po.md   (po's own record of writing it)
  docs/agent-memory/decisions/po-decisions.md (ditto)
Zero code consumers anywhere in the repository. Confirmed independently rather than relayed, and the wider net matters: a scripts/-and-apps/-only grep could have missed a reader in tooling/, .claude/, or a workflow file. It did not — there is none.

WHY THIS BELONGS HERE AND NOT IN A NEW ROW. Identical mechanism, identical failure mode, identical author-trap: a field whose NAME reads as a binding constraint, written in good faith by the agent whose entire job is board correctness, consumed by nothing, and indistinguishable from a working gate by inspecting the board. `blocks` and `co_edit` are the same defect wearing two names. This row's AC 3 — "deliberately author a new reverse-only guard and demonstrate that it is caught, by binding, by a validation error, or by a loud warning" — already covers it verbatim; only the field name changes.

SCOPE ADDITION (small, explicit): whichever remedy this row adopts must dispose of `co_edit` too, and the disposition should be the SAME one chosen for `blocks` — do not fix one and leave the other. Note the asymmetry when choosing: `blocks` has a natural forward-field normalisation target (`blocked_by`/`depends_on`, remedy [b]), whereas `co_edit` has NO existing forward equivalent — there is no "must ship atomically with" primitive in the schema at all. So for `co_edit` the honest menu is narrower: either (i) introduce a real co-edit/atomic-ship primitive that something reads, or (ii) delete the field and force the intent into prose on both rows plus a `depends_on` edge that at least serialises them, or (iii) reject unknown/unread top-level task fields at write time in scripts/orch-apply.sh, which kills this whole class permanently instead of playing whack-a-mole with field names. po's preference, stated as input to ba/architect and NOT as a decision: (iii) is the only option that stops the NEXT invented field, and it is cheap — orch-apply.sh already validates; a known-key allowlist with a loud rejection on unknown keys is a natural extension of the Zod stage. But (iii) has a real migration cost across 658 live rows with many ad-hoc annotation fields (this note's own key included), so it needs measuring before adoption, not assuming.

INTERIM MITIGATION ALREADY APPLIED — DO NOT ASSUME THE BINDING IS UNPROTECTED TODAY. The router, on dispatching FIX-DEVTEAM-BACKGROUND-SPAWN-LOCK-RELEASED-AT-SPAWN-NOT-COMPLETION to architect, passed the co-edit requirement as an explicit MANDATORY instruction in the spawn prompt, including the fact that nothing enforces it. So that specific instance is human-relayed and covered for this dispatch only. It is NOT covered for any future dispatch, re-dispatch, or resume — which is exactly the residual this row exists to close.

TRANSFERABLE LESSON, one line, for this row's eventual findings and for the SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP cross-ref already recorded above: THE COUNT OF DECORATIVE FIELDS IS NOW TWO AND WAS DISCOVERED TWICE IN ONE DAY BY ACCIDENT, BOTH TIMES AUTHORED BY PO. That is evidence the trap is structural and frequently sprung, not a one-off lapse — which raises the value of a class remedy (iii) over per-field cleanup, and is the strongest argument in this row for not settling on remedy [c] (delete-and-forbid) alone.

backlog.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T17:38Z by po from router triage item 5 ("ticker-count three-way disagreement, unresolved"). po RESOLVED the disagreement by probing the runtime rather than comparing files, and what is left after resolving it is this row — a real, live, product-visible defect that the count-comparison was obscuring.

THERE WAS NEVER A THREE-WAY DISAGREEMENT. THE SETS ARE STRICTLY NESTED. po called the RUNTIME `get_watchlist` tool through the gateway — the exact tool both cowork flows call to build WATCHLIST — and diffed all three sets this tick:
    system-map (34, 33 active)  SUBSET  coverage-state (57)  SUBSET  get_watchlist (58)
  get_watchlist \ coverage-state = {MWG}   (exactly one)
  coverage-state \ get_watchlist = {}      (empty)
  system-map     \ get_watchlist = {}      (empty)
No set contains a ticker the larger one lacks. Nothing contradicts anything; two of the three are simply stale or partial VIEWS of one roster.

AUTHORITATIVE ROSTER = runtime `get_watchlist`, 58 tickers, backed by the SQLite `watchlist` table (cf. apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/sector/correlationTools.ts:50-59, `SELECT code FROM watchlist`; tool registered at src/interface/mcp/tools/system/watchlist.ts:309). news-scout's c200 notebook claim of "58" was CORRECT and was wrongly flagged as the outlier by two prior reports — it is the only one of the three numbers that matches what the code actually serves. coverage-state.json (57) is a write-side LEDGER, not a roster, and its one-ticker gap (MWG) self-heals via the coverage-stamp fix; that is handled on FIX-COVERAGE-SWEEP-BLANKET-STAMP-DEAD-TRIGGER and is NOT in scope here.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT: docs/data/system-map.json `.project.watchlist` HAS 34 ENTRIES AND IS MISSING 24 OF THE 58 LIVE WATCHLIST TICKERS. Missing, verbatim from the set-diff:
  ACB ACV BDI CTG D2D DHG DLC GAS GVR HCM HSG HVN JSH MBB MWG NKG POW PPC REE SIS TCH VDC VNH VPB
That list includes ACB, CTG, MBB and VPB — four of Vietnam's largest listed banks — plus GAS, MWG, HVN, ACV, REE, POW, GVR, HCM. This is not a long tail of illiquid names; it is a 41% hole containing several of the highest-impact tickers on the exchange.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC — THE STALE FILE HAS LIVE CONSUMERS, VERIFIED AT SOURCE:
  1. CLAUDE.md instructs EVERY agent: "All structural data (services, agents, zones, channels, sources, watchlist) lives in docs/data/system-map.json. Query with jq — never hardcode values." An agent that obeys this instruction correctly gets 33 active tickers and silently under-covers 24. The project's own canonical anti-hardcode rule currently routes agents to the WRONG roster.
  2. .claude/skills/system-map-query/SKILL.md:106-115 is the canonical query pattern and ships four worked examples all reading `.project.watchlist[]` — the documented-correct way to get the watchlist returns 33.
  3. docs/agents/fb-market-poster/flow/main.md:200 derives its ticker set from `.project.watchlist[] | select(.active==true)` — a PUBLIC-FACING publisher operating on 33 of 58.
  4. apps/frontend/app/domain/market.ts:293 `WATCHLIST_STOCKS` is a COMPILE-TIME constant that mirrors this file (its own docstring says so: "Canonical watchlist — mirrors docs/data/system-map.json project.watchlist"), embedded at build time, never read from FS at runtime. po confirmed ACB/CTG/MBB/VPB/GAS/MWG appear NOWHERE in that file. The dashboard therefore cannot show four of the largest banks in the market.

PRIOR ART — THIS EXACT DIVERGENCE HAS ALREADY CAUSED A MISSED DETECTION ONCE. docs/spikes/SPIKE_1946-crisis-detection-plx-gap.md diagnosed a crisis-detection MISS whose root cause it names as "a watchlist divergence": PLX was absent from `.project.watchlist[]` while present elsewhere. That instance was fixed (po verified PLX is now at index 31 of system-map and present in market.ts) but the CLASS was never closed — the file drifted straight back to a 24-ticker hole. Treat that spike as the impact precedent when sizing this: the demonstrated consequence is a missed market event, not an inaccurate document.

REMEDY — DIRECTION OPEN, ba/architect own HOW. po did NOT choose, but flags the trap: a one-time hand-sync of 24 rows fixes today and guarantees the same drift returns, exactly as it did after SPIKE_1946. Candidates: (i) GENERATE `.project.watchlist` from the `watchlist` table so the file is derived and cannot drift, with the frontend constant regenerated from it in the same step; (ii) keep the file authored but add a CI/audit check asserting `.project.watchlist` set-equals the runtime `get_watchlist` set, failing loud on divergence; (iii) delete `.project.watchlist` outright and repoint CLAUDE.md, the system-map-query skill, fb-market-poster's flow and the frontend at the runtime tool — smallest surface, but the frontend needs a build-time or runtime fetch it does not have today, so cost is real. Whichever is chosen must also correct the stale docstrings that assert the mirror is canonical.

ACCEPTANCE (all RAW):
  1. `jq '[.project.watchlist[].ticker] | length' docs/data/system-map.json` set-equals the runtime `get_watchlist` roster — assert SET EQUALITY, not the number 58. A count check passes on the wrong 58 tickers; the ticker sets must match exactly, both directions.
  2. The frontend surface renders the full roster — ACB, CTG, MBB, VPB specifically present — verified in the SERVED page, not in the source constant (feedback_host_cli_integrity_check_false_ok / feedback_factory_testfirst_primitive_tests_copy_not_served_path: check the served path, not a copy).
  3. NEGATIVE CONTROL, the criterion separating a real fix from a re-sync: add a ticker to the runtime watchlist, then demonstrate the divergence is CAUGHT — by regeneration, by a failing audit, or by a loud warning. A remedy that only reconciles today's 24 leaves the drift mechanism armed and SPIKE_1946 will recur a third time.
  4. CLAUDE.md's "never hardcode, query system-map for watchlist" instruction is either made TRUE or repointed at the real SSOT. Leaving the project's canonical rule pointing at a stale roster is not an acceptable end state.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: the coverage-state ledger and its MWG gap (owned by FIX-COVERAGE-SWEEP-BLANKET-STAMP-DEAD-TRIGGER); the blanket-stamp defect; the Bash-grant transport decision. Do not pull them in — three separate rows, three separate deliverables, one shared symptom of "nobody agreed which list is the list".

backlog.title: cowork spawn-fanout dispatches slot.flow_path, not slot.trigger_prompt — digest-daily is the one slot whose two fields disagree, so every dispatcher fire enters daily-predict.md directly and never evaluates the published:digest-daily:<UTC_DATE> duplicate-claim gate, which lives only in main.md
backlog.root_cause: Four facts, each verified at source by PO 2026-07-28T13:3xZ, not inferred from the report. (1) docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/spawn-fanout.md:192 builds the spawn prompt as `run <slot.flow_path>  slot=<slot.slot_id>` — the dispatched entry point is slot.flow_path; slot.trigger_prompt is never read by the spawn step. (2) docs/data/cowork-schedule.json digest-daily carries flow_path='docs/agents/digest-predict/flow/daily-predict.md' but trigger_prompt='run docs/agents/digest-predict/flow/main.md  slot=digest-daily' — the two fields name DIFFERENT files. Its sibling digest-sunday has both fields naming main.md, so digest-daily is the sole divergent slot on the schedule. (3) The daily dedup gate is 'Step pre-D: DAILY-PREDICT DEDUP GATE' at docs/agents/digest-predict/flow/main.md:15-45, claiming published:digest-daily:<UTC_DATE> with an 86400s TTL. It exists ONLY in main.md. (4) daily-predict.md contains exactly ONE task_claim (line 131) and it is the commit-mutex, not a published marker. THEREFORE every cowork-dispatched digest-daily fire enters daily-predict.md and skips the gate entirely. The gate's own comment states what is lost: it 'protects against cron re-fire, session restart, or dispatcher double-fire producing duplicate claims for the same UTC calendar day' — precisely the protection that is dead on the only path the dispatcher uses.
backlog.deliverable: PREFERRED (general): make spawn-fanout Step 5.2 dispatch slot.trigger_prompt when present, falling back to the composed flow_path form — trigger_prompt is the field literally named for this and is the one a slot author edits to change the entry point. PLUS a consistency assertion so a future slot cannot silently re-introduce the divergence: fail loud (or refuse the slot) when trigger_prompt names a different file than flow_path. ACUTE MITIGATION if the general fix is deferred: point digest-daily's flow_path at main.md so both fields agree — one field, immediate, but it does not stop the next slot from diverging. Do NOT 'fix' this by copying the dedup gate into daily-predict.md: that creates a second copy of a claim gate that must stay byte-identical to the first, which is the duplicate-predicate class scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq was consolidated to kill.
backlog.acceptance: Two consecutive dispatcher fires of digest-daily inside the same UTC calendar day produce ONE set of prediction claims, and the second logs the gate's own already-claimed skip path — proven from the live claim/lock evidence, not from flow prose. Negative control: a first fire of the day still runs (do not turn the gate into a blanket suppressor). Static assertion: every slot in docs/data/cowork-schedule.json has trigger_prompt and flow_path naming the same file, asserted by a test that reads the live schedule (today digest-daily is the only violation — it must be the one that fails before the fix and passes after).

Landing catch-up while this bypass stands means retro-fires can duplicate a day's prediction claims with no arbiter. This row does not depend_on the epic and should land BEFORE or ALONGSIDE it; recorded as a note, not a dep, so it stays independently dispatchable. backlog.title: system-auditor labelled `pdf-extractor at memory limit 98.87% (2.472/2.5 GiB)` as WARN (rank 2) when its own tier-1 ladder maps `peak >97%` to CRITICAL (rank 3): `--severity` is a hand-authored literal with no binding to the measured value, so the dedup layer's escalation bypass (`new_rank > stored_rank`) is structurally unreachable for magnitude-driven conditions — and three improvised dedup_keys for one condition are currently the ONLY reason the 98.87% alert was not suppressed
backlog.root_cause: PREMISE CORRECTION — THE ESCALATING REPORT'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS REFUTED, AND THE REFUTATION IS THE FINDING. The report to PO asserted: `its BUG Telegram was DEDUP-SKIPPED: dedup_key microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY had already been sent at 2026-07-28T14:30:09Z for the BENIGN 85% state ... the key minted while the condition was 'stable plateau, not a defect' now suppresses notification for '20 MiB from OOM and climbing' for the next 7 days.` PO checked the ledger and the signal rows instead of accepting this. It is wrong on the decisive fact. The 14:30:09Z entry did NOT carry the benign 85% state. Live signal_queue row sys-20260728T143010-6ec2, ts=2026-07-28T14:30:10Z, summary verbatim: `pdf-extractor at memory limit 98.87% (2.472/2.5 GiB) — sustained after OCR workload`. The 14:30:09Z Telegram WAS the near-cap alert, and it WAS sent. What the 14:34:57Z emit hit was a 4-minute-later re-observation of the SAME state (98.84% vs 98.87%) under the SAME key — a textbook intra-cycle duplicate, and the router itself independently classified it as one on the row: `router_dedup_note: INTRA-CYCLE DUPLICATE of sys-20260728T143010-6ec2 (same sweep, same pdf-extractor condition, 98.84 vs 98.87). Triage as ONE.` THE DEDUP GATE BEHAVED CORRECTLY. No escalation was swallowed. Filing the reported bug as reported would have `fixed` the one component in the chain that worked. LEDGER TIMELINE, read from docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json at 2026-07-28T14:44Z, which is what the claim should have been checked against: `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:PDF-MEM-01` ts=2026-07-28T12:49:39Z sev=2 | `mem_pressure:pdf-extractor:A-30-PDF-EXTRACTOR` ts=2026-07-28T13:12:18Z sev=2 (this is the 85.54% plateau — archived signal row sys-20260728T131219-3fca, `pdf-extractor memory 85.54% of 2.5 GiB (2.138 GiB) — stable plateau`) | `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY` ts=2026-07-28T14:30:09Z sev=2 (this is the 98.87%). Three keys, one condition, 101 minutes, all rank 2. DEFECT 1 — SEVERITY IS A HAND-AUTHORED LABEL, NOT A FUNCTION OF THE MEASUREMENT. scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh `_severity_rank()` collapses to `CRITICAL) echo 3 ;; HIGH|WARN) echo 2 ;; MED|INFO) echo 1 ;; *) echo 1`, ranking whatever string the calling agent typed into `--severity`. docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md clause 5 states the policy the label was supposed to follow: `verdict=="ESCALATE", reason contains "OOMKilled=true" -> CRITICAL` / `reason contains "peak >97%" -> CRITICAL` / `reason contains "no reclamation dip" (>93% baseline case) -> WARN`. 98.87% is a `peak >97%` reading; the policy says CRITICAL (rank 3); the emit said WARN (rank 2). That ladder is prose in a markdown file, enforceable only by an LLM remembering to read it, and the tier-2 sweep that produced this emit does not read it at all — there is no tier2 flow file (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/ contains only main.md, tier1-probe.md, page-freshness.md). Nothing in the emit script can detect that `--severity WARN` contradicts a summary reading `98.87% of 2.5 GiB`. CONTROL CASE, SAME AUDITOR, SAME SWEEP, MINUTES APART — this is why the diagnosis is producer-side and not gate-side: sbv_fx DID escalate its label across the identical window, sys-20260728T142957-693e ts=14:29:57Z severity=HIGH `sbv_fx stale 43min (SLA 30min)` then sys-20260728T143455-6a8a ts=14:34:55Z severity=CRITICAL `sbv_fx stale 47min (check B-02-SBV)`. Rank 2 -> rank 3 on the same sweep, which would fire the bypass exactly as designed. One condition varied its label with the measurement; the other did not. The gate is common to both. DEFECT 2 — DEDUP-KEY NAMESPACE DRIFT, and it is currently MASKING defect 1. docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:208 prescribes `"dedup_key":"microservice_degraded:<service_id>:<A-xx>"` with the worked example at :93 `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-20`; the canonical key here is `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30`. The call sites instead improvised `PDF-MEM-01`, `A-30-PDF-EXTRACTOR` under a `mem_pressure:` category prefix that appears in no documented category set, and `A-30-MEMORY`. THE CONSEQUENCE IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS ROW: because `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY` was a BRAND-NEW key at 14:30:09Z, `_ledger_prune_and_lookup` found no entry, took the `if [ -z "$LEDGER_ENTRY_TS" ]` branch, and SENT. Had the keys been correctly normalised, the 98.87% emit would have collided with the 13:12:18Z 85.54% entry under one canonical key, compared 2 > 2, evaluated false, and been SKIP-dedup'd — the exact failure the escalating report described, which has not happened yet but WOULD have. Key drift is accidentally load-bearing today. SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT THAT FALLS OUT OF THAT: shipping the key-normalisation half of this row WITHOUT the severity-derivation half MANUFACTURES the reported bug. They must land together, or severity-derivation must land first. DEFECT 3 — PO RE-ESCALATION THRESHOLDS HAVE NO MACHINE-READABLE HOME, which is why PO learned of the crossing by hand. PO's 2026-07-28T13:12Z disposition on sys-20260728T131219-3fca reads `RESOLVED, no mint, MONITOR with a named re-escalation threshold (not a silent file-and-forget) ... RE-ESCALATE, and mint then, if ANY of: crosses 95% of cap, OOMKilled=true, or RestartCount climbs.` That text lives in a `po_disposition_20260728` string field on a signal row that has since been cold-evicted to docs/data/orch/archive/2026-07.json. No detector, no emit path, and no bridge reads that field. When 98.87% was measured at 14:30Z, every participant independently re-derived a severity from scratch and every one of them landed on WARN — the auditor's label, the router's corroboration (`SEVERITY: WARN is right — failure mode is OOM -> docker restart -> recovery, not permanent damage`), and the router's trend note (`No push notification sent — the router already spent one push today on a memory claim it had to retract, and a second for a self-recovering WARN would be noise`). Each judgement is individually defensible. None of them had access to the fact that PO had pre-committed 95%-of-cap as the mint trigger four hours earlier. NOT A DEFECT, CHECKED AND CLEARED — the anomaly-task-bridge did not fail: .claude/skills/anomaly-task-bridge/SKILL.md ATB-1 collects `to == "po"`, `status == "NEW"`, `row.ts < now() - 2h`, so at 14:47Z both rows (17 and 12 minutes old) are correctly grace-window-pending, not dropped; they would surface at ~16:30Z. The 2h gate is a deliberate transient-suppression design and this row does not propose changing it — but note that for a service with ~20 MiB of headroom, a 2h grace and a WARN label compose into a 2h blind spot, which is a further argument for defect 1 rather than for touching the gate.
backlog.deliverable: (a) MAKE SEVERITY DERIVABLE FROM THE MEASUREMENT, not merely assertable. Add a measured-value contract to `emit-audit-signal.sh` (exact shape is the implementer's call — e.g. `--metric-value <n> --metric-warn <n> --metric-critical <n>`, or a required `metric` object inside `--detail-json`) and rank from it when present. The derived rank must WIN over the free-text `--severity` string for bypass purposes. backlog.status_note:
MECHANICALLY VERIFIED (not inferred) from list_unresolved_reports() this tick: 37 unresolved [sla-monitor] CRITICAL breach alerts for signal_quality_audit, every hour from 2026-07-26T16:30:03Z (stale=73217min) through 2026-07-28T16:00:09Z (stale=76067min, still climbing), threshold constant at 2880min (48h) throughout — none marked resolved. ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS, read at source, TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS COMPOUNDING:
(1) MISCLASSIFICATION: apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/freshnessSlaMonitorJob.ts:97 comments signal_quality_audit as "event-driven; 48h SLA" — but cronConfig.ts:129 + schedulerJobTable.ts:227-233 register it as monthlySignalQualityAuditJob, cron `0 0 1 * *` (1st-of-month only). A monthly-cadence job graded against a 48h SLA is CRITICAL for ~28 of every ~30 days even when working correctly — same defect class as FIX-SLA-BCTC-THRESHOLD-TRACKS-STALENESS-NOT-CONSTANT (this file, adjacent metric) though the specific mechanism differs (there: threshold itself computed, not constant; here: a correct constant threshold applied to the wrong cadence class).
(2) POSSIBLY-DEAD JOB ON TOP OF THAT: even a perfectly-functioning monthly cron caps observed staleness at ~31 days; 76067min = 52.8 days and climbing means the job has NOT fired since ~2026-06-06 — it should have fired 2026-07-01 and did not. schedulerJobTable.ts:227 registers this job with `recoverMissedExecutions: false` (explicit opt-out, code comment: "recovery is opt-out here until a T4 dedup guard is added ... in a future sprint") — if the mcp-server process was down/restarting at exactly 2026-07-01T00:00 UTC (this repo rebuilds/restarts containers frequently per ops history), that month's run is silently and permanently skipped, with zero recovery and zero distinguishing alert from "normal quiet month".
REMEDY (direction, not fully prescribed): (a) give signal_quality_audit its own SLA class/threshold sized to the monthly cadence (e.g. ~35-40d grace, mirroring how bond_maturity already gets a 168h/7d threshold for its own weekly cadence in the SAME file) instead of the shared 48h "event-driven" bucket; (b) verify at source whether the 2026-07-01 fire actually ran (check logs/audit table for a row near that date) — if missed, this is the concrete, datable instance the code comment already anticipated, and argues for pulling the deferred T4 dedup/recovery guard forward rather than leaving it another sprint.
ACCEPTANCE: (1) signal_quality_audit threshold no longer fires CRITICAL merely for being mid-cycle on a working monthly cadence — assert against a fixture where MAX(created_at) is 20 days old (should NOT breach) and 40 days old (SHOULD breach); (2) confirm/refute at source whether the 2026-07-01 run actually executed — state the finding in the closing report, do not guess; (3) if confirmed missed, either backfill a corrective run or file the recoverMissedExecutions follow-up explicitly (do not silently leave both defects unaddressed).

The defect it exists to prevent REPRODUCED IN PRODUCTION today against PO's own triage commit — see FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD .po_disposition_20260728 for the verbatim sequence and the forensic commit (09ae11440, 5 of 7 files foreign). Its parent is BLOCKED on this row, so every day this sits undispatched the parent's block is also load-bearing. TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS THAT THE LIVE REPRODUCTION ADDS AND THAT THE ORIGINAL SCOPE DOES NOT STATE. (1) The hook MUST bind the INV-GATEWAY-1 exempt population (dev-*/qa/ba/pm/architect specialists). They never call commit-mutex by design (SKILL.md:4-8), so any guard implemented inside the skill is unreachable for exactly the agents that caused this. A git pre-commit hook is the correct layer precisely because it is transport-agnostic and cannot be opted out of. (2) The detection predicate cannot be 'verify the index before commit'. PO's 3b verify returned CLEAN (exactly 5 own paths, zero foreign) and the sweep still happened, because the peer committed in the gap between 3b and 3c. The hook must evaluate at commit time, comparing the commit's actual file set against the committing agent's declared own-paths, and fail loud on foreign inclusion — a snapshot taken any earlier is a TOCTOU read.

ready.title: SPIKE: sweep for count-threshold gates whose input has a permanent floor above the threshold — a gate that always fires stops discriminating while still reporting that it fired
ready.question: Which other count-threshold gates across flows, scripts and crons are evaluated against an input with a structural floor at or above their threshold, so that they fire unconditionally and can no longer detect the condition they exist to detect?
ready.po_rationale_20260721T1724: TWO independent instances of this exact shape were found in ONE dev-team tick (2026-07-21T17:07Z), by different routes, in unrelated subsystems. That is what justifies a class sweep rather than two isolated fixes. A threshold whose input has a floor above it is strictly WORSE than no gate: it is false assurance, and it reports success every time it fires.
ready.confirmed_instance_1: dev-team drain guard — docs/agents/dev-team/flow/drain-signals.md:7 fires on `ls docs/signals/*.json | wc -l > 50`, against a permanent structural inbox floor of 54 undrainable files (46 cowork-team state files, 7 price_anomaly, 1 outage). Confirmed structural: unchanged by a SUCCESSFUL drain in the same tick. Already owned by CLEAN-COWORK-DISPATCHER-TELEMETRY-DRAIN-DIR (ready/P1) — DO NOT re-mint or re-fix, cite it as instance 1 only.
ready.confirmed_instance_2: cowork SILENT gate — scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-preflight.sh Step 7 lines 243-252 requires signal_count -eq 0, and signal_count is permanently >=1 because cowork-addressed rows are never marked READ. Defeats a stated ~80%-of-ticks LLM-read optimisation every 15 minutes, self-sustainingly. Cause owned by SPIKE-COWORK-DRAIN-BODY-NOT-EXECUTING-ON-WORK-TICKS — DO NOT re-fix, cite as instance 2 only.
ready.scope: Enumerate count/threshold predicates in docs/agents/**/flow/*.md, scripts/agents-flow/*.sh, scripts/*.sh and cron/scheduler configs. For each: identify the input set, determine whether it has a floor (undrainable/immortal/monotonic members), and compare that floor to the threshold. Report gates where floor >= threshold (SATURATED, always fires) and — the mirror case, worth catching in the same pass — gates where the input can never reach the threshold (DEAD, never fires).
ready.explicitly_not_in_scope: Do NOT fix instances 1 and 2; they have owners. Do NOT change any gate found by this sweep — output is the inventory plus a per-gate severity call. Fixes are separate rows so each can be verified independently.
ready.acceptance: Findings doc listing every count-threshold gate examined with: file:line, threshold, input set, measured or reasoned floor/ceiling, and verdict SATURATED / DEAD / HEALTHY. Include the gates that came back HEALTHY — a sweep that only reports hits cannot be distinguished from a sweep that stopped early.
ready.generalisation_to_test: Worth stating explicitly in the findings: a gate is only meaningful if its input can actually cross the threshold in BOTH directions. If any such gate is found to lack a regression test asserting that, say so — that is the durable fix for the class.
ready.router_finding_dead_gate: ROUTER 2026-07-21T17:41:58Z — THIRD INSTANCE, and it is a DEAD gate rather than a saturated one, which this row explicitly asks for. scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh: on the TIER-1 path run_probe() is called with NO suppress_heartbeat argument (line 295 takes it as the first positional; line 324 writes the heartbeat unless it equals that literal). So the probe WRITES docs/data/auditor-tier1-last-healthy.json on ALL_GREEN, and the cron LLM prompt then reads that same file back and computes an age of ~0 every time. The prompt branch [ALL_GREEN but heartbeat age over 60min] is therefore UNREACHABLE. On the FAILURE path it is redundant instead, because verdict=FAILURE already triggers the spawn by itself. Net: the freshness guard contributes nothing on tier 1 in either verdict state. Router observed it live — probe wrote 17:39:55Z, computed age 0 min, at 2026-07-21T17:41:58Z.
ready.router_finding_fix_pattern_already_exist: DO NOT DESIGN A NEW REMEDY — the exact fix already exists in the SAME FILE for tiers 2/3, shipped 2026-07-16 as auditor-signal-loop-P1. That change suppresses the run_probe heartbeat write for tier 2/3 and computes freshness from the PRE-EXISTING value captured BEFORE run_probe runs. The header of that file (lines ~96-118) names the defect in the same terms this row uses: age was always ~0 because it was computed from a value this same pre-gate had just written, making SKIP-SPAWN unconditional on green and the [ALL_GREEN + stale heartbeat -> SPAWN] branch dead code. Tier 1 was deliberately left 100% unchanged (line 80) and so still carries it.
ready.router_scope_boundary: Router did NOT determine whether tier 1 needs this guard at all. Tier 1 runs 6 live checks every tick, so its green is not passive in the way tier 2/3 green is. The honest options are: [a] port the tier-2/3 suppression to tier 1, or [b] delete the branch from the cron prompt as genuinely unnecessary and stop implying a check that does not happen. That is a design call for whoever works this row, not a router call. What is NOT acceptable is leaving a prompt instruction that reads as a live safety gate while being unreachable.
ready.router_healthy_gate_positive_control: POSITIVE CONTROL, per this row requirement to list healthy gates so the sweep is distinguishable from one that stopped early: the tier-1 heartbeat WRITE condition itself is healthy and NOT saturated — the script writes only on ALL_GREEN, downgrades to FAILURE if the write itself fails (never claims green without a verified write), and leaves the file untouched on FAILURE so age genuinely grows. Router verified this BEFORE going looking for the defect, so the finding is not the product of a search that only reports hits.
ready.po_finding_instance_6_20260721T1845: PO 2026-07-21T18:45Z — SIXTH INSTANCE, and a DEAD gate (the mirror case this row explicitly asks the sweep to catch), in a NEW sub-class the first five did not cover. Prior instances all concern a COUNT compared to a threshold. This one is an AGE comparison defeated by a MISSING INPUT: docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md:491 resets stale-crashed rows on head.updated_at >= 24h. SPIKE-BCTC-EXTRACTION-DORMANT-MASS-ENRICHFAIL-FLOOD sat IN_PROGRESS from 2026-07-16T21:00:34Z with NO updated_at field at all, so the predicate had nothing to evaluate and the reset was unreachable for exactly the row that most needed it — five days, and it was the binding WIP constraint on the whole board. GENERALISATION WORTH TESTING IN THE SWEEP: extend scope beyond 'floor >= threshold' to 'predicate whose INPUT FIELD can be absent'. A comparison against null/absent is not merely false — it is silently, permanently false, and unlike a saturated gate it produces no output at all to notice. Sub-class to enumerate: every gate reading .updated_at / .created_at / .started_at / .last_* where the field is optional in the schema and is not backfilled on write. Note that scripts/orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs deliberately does NOT backfill existing null rows (documented in its own header), so this sub-class is live and populated today, not hypothetical. PO ALSO OBSERVED, worth one line in the findings doc: head.wip and head.wip_max were BOTH null live while the board was in fact enforcing a limit of 2 — an invariant carried entirely by convention with no encoded value for any gate to read. wip_max has now been set to 2; wip is deliberately left null and computed, per the standing rule that conservation totals are computed and not stored. DO NOT FIX instance 6 here — the row has been moved to ready/TODO and the class fix belongs to whichever row this sweep spawns.
ready.router_instance_7_empty_scanset_pass: ROUTER 2026-07-21T19:04:36Z — INSTANCE 7, surfaced by qa during FIX-ORCHSTATE-UPDATED-AT-WRITE-PATH review and re-verified at source by router. THIRD SUB-CLASS: not floor-above-threshold (1-5), not comparison-against-absent-field (6), but A GUARD THAT EMITS PASS ON AN EMPTY SCAN SET. scripts/audits/mock-guard.sh in --files mode filters the caller-supplied file list at line 70 with the regex '\.(ts|tsx|js|py|go)$'. .sh, .mjs and .jq do not match, so for any task touching ONLY those extensions file_list is empty, and lines 74-77 print '[mock-guard] No production source files to scan. PASS.' and exit 0. That output is indistinguishable from 'scanned and found nothing'. Both rows reviewed this tick hit it: row 1's central artifact is scripts/orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs and row 2's is a .sh/.jq pair, so the guard reported PASS for precisely the changes it structurally cannot see. QA disclosed this rather than banking the green, and manually read the changed files instead — that disclosure is the only reason it is on the board.
ready.router_instance_7_scope_correction: ROUTER CHECKED ITS OWN FIRST HYPOTHESIS AND IT WAS WRONG — recording the correction so the next reader does not re-derive the bad version. Router initially suspected .js files pass the line-70 gate but are then dropped by the --include=*.ts/tsx/py/go flags in run_grep, which would be worse (counted in-scope, silently unscanned) and would have implicated scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.js. That is FALSE. Read run_grep at lines 92-105: the --include flags apply ONLY to the full-backstop recursive branch; the --files branch runs plain 'grep -nE PATTERN $SCAN_TARGET' against the explicit list, so .js IS scanned in --files mode. The real defect is narrower than the first guess: it is the line-70 extension filter alone, and it affects .sh/.mjs/.jq only.
ready.router_instance_7_fix_boundary: Router did NOT choose the remedy. The honest options: [a] widen the line-70 filter to include .sh/.mjs/.jq (cheap, but the HARD/CAUTION patterns at line 34 were authored for TS/Py/Go idioms and may misfire or under-fire on shell/jq); [b] keep the scope but make the empty-scanset path emit SKIPPED / exit non-zero-distinct rather than 'PASS', so a caller can tell 'nothing to check' from 'checked, clean'. [b] is the smaller change and fixes the FALSE GREEN even if the scope stays narrow; [a] without [b] still leaves every future unlisted extension silently green. What is NOT acceptable is leaving a line that prints PASS when nothing was examined.
ready.router_instance_8_self_satisfying_freshn: INSTANCE 8 — FOURTH SUB-CLASS: A GATE WHOSE PRECONDITION IS ESTABLISHED BY THE THING IT GATES. Surfaced by router across four consecutive tier-1 cron ticks and verified at source. The tier-1 cron prompt carries a passive-health-masking guard worded 'check every tick, even after ALL_GREEN — stale green is not green': read docs/data/auditor-tier1-last-healthy.json .last_healthy_at, compute age, and spawn system-auditor if age > 60min. But scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh WRITES that same heartbeat file on its own ALL_GREEN branch. So on the ALL_GREEN path the file was authored seconds earlier by the very run being evaluated, and the measured age is always ~0 by construction (observed 0min at the 19:39:56Z tick). The guard can only ever trip on the FAILURE path, where the verdict already forces a spawn unaided. It therefore contributes exactly nothing on every path it can take, while reading as a satisfied staleness check in the tick log.
ready.router_instance_8_distinction_20260721T1: HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM INSTANCE 7, so the sweep does not collapse them. Instance 7 (mock-guard empty scanset) is a gate that examines an EMPTY INPUT and reports PASS. Instance 8 examines a NON-empty input and reports PASS, but the input is a value the gate's own subject just wrote — the scan set is fine, the OBSERVATION IS NOT INDEPENDENT OF THE OBSERVED. Same false-green surface, different mechanism, and they need different repairs: instance 7 wants a distinct SKIPPED/empty-set exit, instance 8 wants either an independent freshness source or deletion of the branch. Tiers 2 and 3 reportedly carry a suppression that tier-1 lacks; porting it is one candidate fix, but router did NOT verify that suppression at source and it must not be assumed to exist.
ready.router_instance_8_fix_boundary_20260721T: ROUTER DID NOT CHOOSE THE REMEDY. Honest options: [a] delete the heartbeat-age branch from the tier-1 cron prompt and stop advertising a staleness check that cannot fire — smallest change, loses nothing real; [b] have the probe write the heartbeat ONLY on a path distinct from the one the guard reads, so age reflects health persistence rather than probe recency; [c] port whatever suppression tiers 2/3 use, AFTER verifying it exists and is not the same self-satisfying shape one level up. What is NOT acceptable is leaving a prompt that instructs an operator to check staleness against a value the check's own subject authored moments before.
ready.router_sibling_harness_break_20260721T19: ADJACENT FINDING — NOT A NEW SWEEP INSTANCE, BUT THE SAME FALSE-GREEN FAMILY, ROUTED HERE FOR PO TO PLACE. Surfaced by developer during CLEAN-COWORK-DISPATCHER-TELEMETRY-DRAIN-DIR and independently re-verified by router at source. scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.test.js:256 builds its sandbox by copying a FIXED LIST of orch helpers: ['scripts/orch-apply.sh','scripts/orch-validate.mjs','scripts/orch-conservation-check.mjs']. Commit a5d079663 (FIX-ORCHSTATE-UPDATED-AT-WRITE-PATH, same day) ADDED scripts/orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs and MODIFIED scripts/orch-apply.sh to invoke it — without adding the new file to that copy list. So orch-apply.sh inside the sandbox now calls a file that is not there, and the makeOrchRefHarness scenario CRASHES THE WHOLE TEST PROCESS, taking every later scenario in the file with it. developer confirmed via git stash that this predates its own change, declined to fix it as out-of-scope, and worked around it by running a truncated copy through the 15 pre-existing scenarios that precede the break. Router endorses the scope call. WHY IT BELONGS NEAR THIS SWEEP: a fix in file A silently disabled a test suite in file B, and nobody noticed — which means that suite was not run after a5d079663 landed. The AC7 golden-stdout regression guard for the drain has therefore been unguarded since that commit. Distinct from instances 1-8 in mechanism (this is a broken fixture, not a gate reporting PASS on a degenerate input) but identical in consequence: an assertion nobody can see is failing. Fix is one array entry; the coverage question behind it is not. PO to rule whether this folds here or needs its own row — ROUTER DID NOT MINT.
ready.po_ruling_harness_break_split_20260721T2: RULING 3 — SPLIT, NOT FOLDED. The drain-signals.test.js harness break gets its OWN row for the code fix (FIX-DRAIN-TEST-HARNESS-ORCH-HELPER-COPY-LIST, ready/P0/XS) and this SPIKE inherits ONLY the coverage question. Rationale: router correctly identified the mechanisms as distinct — a gate reporting PASS on a degenerate input is not the same failure as a fixture that cannot construct itself — and the consequences diverge on cost. The code fix is one array entry and must not wait behind a 120-minute timeboxed sweep; the coverage question genuinely belongs to a sweep. Folding would have held a one-line fix hostage to an investigation. ADDED TO THIS SPIKE'S SCOPE, as a second question: which OTHER test suites are silently not running? The generalisable defect is that a test file's fixture depends on a hardcoded manifest of sibling files, so an unrelated commit can disable it with no failing signal — and CI stayed green because the suite's own crash is indistinguishable from it not being wired into CI at all. Determine (i) whether drain-signals.test.js is in any CI path, (ii) how many other suites build sandboxes from hardcoded file lists, and (iii) whether a suite that exits non-zero anywhere is actually observed by anything.
ready.po_ruling_instance_8_20260721T2050: RULING 4 — REMEDY CHOSEN: NONE OF THE THREE ROUTER OFFERED. Router offered [a] delete the branch, [b] write the heartbeat on a distinct path, [c] port the tier-2/3 suppression. PO verified all three at source and the answer is [d] RELOCATE THE READER. Findings that forced this: (1) [c] IS VERIFIED TO EXIST — run_tiered_probe() at auditor-tier1-probe.sh:419-467 reads pre_existing_lh BEFORE run_probe() and passes the literal suppress_heartbeat flag, so it is genuinely independent, NOT the same self-satisfying shape one level up. Router flagged this as unverified and refused to assume it; that caution was right, and the suppression is now confirmed real. (2) HOWEVER [c] MUST NOT BE PORTED TO TIER 1 AS WORDED — it would convert a dead gate into a SATURATED one, the exact mirror defect this SPIKE exists to catch. The tier-2/3 suppression is only safe because a DISTINCT writer exists: docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:730 writes the heartbeat, and that block is gated on AUDIT_TIER being 2 or 3, with tier-1 explicitly excluded in its own inline comment. There is NO tier-1 heartbeat writer anywhere else in the repo (verified by full-tree grep across sh/md/mjs/js). Suppress the probe write on tier 1 and nothing ever writes the file: age grows without bound, the branch fires EVERY tick, and system-auditor spawns every 30min forever. That is a live token cost, not a cosmetic regression. (3) [a] delete is CORRECT for the false-green defect itself. Tier-1 green is not passive: 6 real shell checks run live every tick, so the stale-green-is-not-green rationale that justified the tier-2/3 fix does not transfer to tier 1. Deleting loses no live signal — corroborated independently by roughly 20 real tier-1 system-auditor notebook commits on 2026-07-21 alone, so tier-1 audits are demonstrably not being suppressed by this gate in practice either. (4) BUT DELETION ALONE DROPS A REAL AND CURRENTLY UNOWNED CAPABILITY, so [a] is not sufficient by itself. The one thing a heartbeat-age check can legitimately detect is TIER-1 CRON DORMANCY (a gap between ticks). PO HYPOTHESISED that orch-sentinel OH-3 already owned this and CHECKED — THE HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG, recorded here so the next reader does not re-derive the bad version: dim-oh3-auditor-blindspot.md:41-47 OH-3.4 does cat all three heartbeat files, but it checks their SHAPE (bare last_healthy_at vs a richer per-dimension shape), is severity INFO, and never computes an age. OH-3.1/3.2/3.3 cover probe-coverage diff, VPS route drift and AUDIT_TIER=4 presence — none of them read heartbeat age. So dormancy detection is genuinely unowned today.
ready.po_ruling_instance_8_remedy_shape_202607: THE REMEDY IS A RELOCATION, NOT A DELETION AND NOT A PORT. The defect in instance 8 is that THE OBSERVER IS NOT INDEPENDENT OF THE OBSERVED. The repair that actually restores that property is to move the READER to a vantage point outside the thing it measures, rather than to change the WRITER. Concretely: delete the heartbeat-age branch from the tier-1 cron prompt — it cannot ever work there, because a cron that is not running does not evaluate its own guard, so the tier-1 cron is structurally incapable of detecting its own dormancy — and add the age check to orch-sentinel as a new OH-3.5, where an independent agent on a different schedule reads it. This is the same structural argument already written at dim-oh3-auditor-blindspot.md:6-9 for why auditor blind-spot checks live in orch-sentinel rather than inside system-auditor; instance 8 is another case of that same principle and the file already states it, so this is applying an existing repo invariant, not inventing one. OWNER SPLIT IS TWO-PARTY AND MUST NOT BE COLLAPSED: developer edits the files; ROUTER must then re-arm the crons. Router owns the arming surface — .claude/skills/cron-detect-loop/register.md is a REGISTRATION SOURCE, not the live cron. The live tier-1 cron already carries the old prompt baked into its own definition, so a developer edit to register.md changes NOTHING live until the crons are re-registered via the /cron-detect-loop skill. A row that stopped at the file edit would be doc-only prose masquerading as an executable fix — precisely the failure mode standing memory feedback_verify_executable_not_flowdoc_prose warns about. Minted as FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-FRESHNESS-CHECK-RELOCATE-TO-SENTINEL (ready/P2/S). This SPIKE retains instance 8 as a catalogued instance; it no longer carries the remedy, and instance 8 is CLOSED for triage purposes — it must not be re-surfaced as an open observation on future ticks.

ready.po_instance_10_coldevict_trigger_action_:
PO 2026-07-25T14:50Z — INSTANCE 10, a SATURATED gate (this row's primary class), and it carries a CORRECTION to the instance_9_closed bounded check above. scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:368 fires the Step 5.5 cold-eviction backstop on `done_n > 10`. Live done_n=16 and the other three disjuncts are all 0, so this single term fires every dev-team tick. The action it fires can never reduce done_n, because orch-cold-evict.sh:242-247 evicts a done row only when it is BOTH beyond keep_n AND older than 7 days: the trigger is a COUNT axis, the action is a COUNT-AND-AGE axis. PO replayed the predicate on the live board — n_evict_done=0, with ranks 0-9 failing the rank gate and ranks 10-15 failing the age gate, so every row fails exactly one gate and none can ever satisfy both. --dry-run confirms 'Byte reduction: 0 bytes'.

WHY THE EARLIER BOUNDED CHECK MISSED IT, recorded so the next reader does not conclude this file was already cleared: instance_9_closed states the architect's sweep found orch-cold-evict.sh to be 'REPORTING counters, not firing gates, so out of this class'. That verdict is CORRECT for the file it examined — the additive sums inside orch-cold-evict.sh really are report counters. But the firing gate for this instance is NOT in that file; it is in scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh, a caller the additive-pattern grep did not cover. The lesson generalises and belongs in the findings doc: WHEN A SCRIPT IS SIDE-EFFECTING, ITS FIRING GATE MAY LIVE IN A DIFFERENT FILE FROM ITS ACTION, so a per-file sweep for gate patterns will systematically miss trigger/action pairs that straddle a file boundary. The sweep must enumerate CALLERS of side-effecting scripts, not only predicates within them.

NEW SUB-CLASS FOR THE INVENTORY, distinct from sub-classes 1-4 already catalogued here (floor-above-threshold; comparison-against-absent-field; PASS-on-empty-scanset; observer-not-independent-of-observed). This is SUB-CLASS 5: TRIGGER AND ACTION EVALUATED ON DIFFERENT AXES. The gate's input is not saturated by a floor and not absent — it is simply a quantity the action is not capable of changing. Enumeration rule to add to the sweep scope: for every gate that fires a side-effecting action, ask whether the action's own predicate can move the gate's input. If it cannot, the gate is unclearable and will fire forever regardless of thresholds. This is cheaper to test than measuring floors, and it catches cases a floor analysis cannot see.

THE INSTANCE. Notebook size is governed by two caps on the same files. The LINE cap (200) has both a detector and an automatic actuator: scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh is a PostToolUse hook that drops the oldest "## " section in a loop until the file is back under cap. The BYTE cap (12000 = 200 * 60 bytes/line, shipped as TE-T24) has a detector only: scripts/agents-flow/context-bloat-backstop.sh:119-123 measures wc -c, emits a signal, and stops. There is no byte actuator anywhere. The pruner's early-exit (:135) and loop-break (:174) are both line-only and it never calls wc -c. Consequence: the line cap is self-healing and permanently satisfied, agents satisfy it by writing DENSER LINES, and bytes grow without bound. alert-commander.md runs 632 bytes/line against a 60 bytes/line budget — 10.5x — while sitting comfortably under the line cap at 190L. 18 of the notebooks are over the byte cap today. Here the actuator IS fully capable of clearing the byte breach — dropping a section reduces lines and bytes together — it simply HALTS TOO EARLY, at a setpoint on the other axis. Sub-class 5 needs a new action; sub-class 7 needs only a corrected stopping condition. Diagnostic question that separates them: "can the action move the detector's input at all?" No -> sub-class 5. Yes, but it stops before the detector is satisfied -> sub-class 7.

ready.defect: The tier-1 cron prompt (.claude/skills/cron-detect-loop/register.md:84) instructs: read docs/data/auditor-tier1-last-healthy.json .last_healthy_at, compute age, and spawn system-auditor if age > 60min — worded as a passive-health guard, check every tick even after ALL_GREEN, stale green is not green. But scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh writes that same heartbeat file on its own ALL_GREEN branch (_write_heartbeat, called at line 325 with no suppress flag on the tier-1 path). On ALL_GREEN the file was authored seconds earlier by the very run being evaluated, so measured age is ~0 by construction — observed 0min across seven consecutive router ticks, most recently heartbeat 20:41:25Z against a 20:41 read. The branch can only trip on the FAILURE path, where verdict=FAILURE already forces the spawn unaided. ready.why_the_obvious_fixes_are_wrong: DO NOT port the tier-2/3 suppression to tier 1. Equally, DO NOT merely delete the branch and stop: that silently drops cron-dormancy detection, which is currently unowned (orch-sentinel OH-3.4 reads the heartbeat files but checks SHAPE only, severity INFO, and never computes an age).

So OH-3.5 as specified ships a FLAPPING false positive, not a permanent one. That is materially different to sequence against and is arguably harder to debug — it will have cleared itself before anyone investigates, and it will re-fire without a code change. Design OH-3.5 with an explicit consecutive-miss / dedup window rather than a single-sample age read, and still land the router re-arm in .ownership_two_party before or with it. Do NOT "fix" this by porting suppress_heartbeat to tier-1 or by dropping the AUDIT_TIER 2/3 gate on the main.md:748 heartbeat write — .why_the_obvious_fixes_are_wrong already rejects that direction.

(4) WHAT STILL STANDS:

  - Two distinct scripts, similar names, opposite contracts: the notebook's raw-probe block is emitted by docs/agents/system-auditor/probe.sh:26, which writes NO heartbeat; the heartbeat writer is scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh.   - .ownership_two_party + AC(4) remain the crux: register.md is a registration source, not the live cron. Read the LIVE cron definition back after re-arm.

(5) METHOD WARNING for whoever picks this up — this triage hit the same failure class THREE times: an artifact of the MEASUREMENT APPARATUS read as a property of the SYSTEM. (i) router read a raw-probe banner emitted by the wrong script as proof the heartbeat writer ran; (ii) po read git history of a dirty file as proof no writer existed; (iii) po counted a write that landed inside po's own investigation window as a tick observation. ready.title: Cold-evict auto-commit captures a live peer WIP inside the same hot file it legitimately stages — a within-file capture that pathspec discipline and the sweep-guard hook both structurally miss
ready.origin: Router observation router_coldevict_sweep_recurrence_20260721T2020 on CLEAN-COWORK-DISPATCHER-TELEMETRY-DRAIN-DIR, plus PO field verification of the incident at 2026-07-21T20:14:18Z where commit e3e5c9f92 absorbed PO live board work (4 rows + 20 annotation keys) under a cold-evict message. Harm that time was ATTRIBUTION-ONLY — PO verified all three transforms landed complete and a duplicate-ID scan returned none — but that outcome depended on PO noticing and on a mid-run warning, neither of which is a mechanism.
ready.po_correction_router_candidates: PO RE-VERIFIED ROUTER THREE CANDIDATE FIXES AT SOURCE AND TWO OF THEM DO NOT SURVIVE. (a) Router proposed the evictor should TAKE commit-mutex:main. IT ALREADY DOES — dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:366-379 _step55_cold_evict_and_commit claims task_id commit-mutex:main, task_kind commit-mutex, ttl 120s, and returns early skipping the whole tick when the claim fails. This candidate is already implemented and is not the gap. (b) Router proposed the evictor should commit ONLY the paths it evicted. IT ALREADY DOES, and it would not have helped: git show --stat e3e5c9f92 reports exactly ONE file changed (docs/data/orch/orch-state.json), and line 415 stages exactly two explicit paths (ORCH_STATE_PATH and the archive file). orch-state.json IS the path it legitimately evicted — the peer work was INSIDE it. No pathspec discipline can separate the eviction transform from peer rows in the same file. (c) Only router third candidate — skip the auto-commit when the file is peer-dirty — engages the actual mechanism, and it is also the cheapest.
ready.actual_mechanism: The mutex serialises COMMITTERS, but PO and every other board writer are not committers — they are WRITERS, and they go through scripts/orch-apply.sh, which PO verified contains NO task_claim and NO commit-mutex participation whatsoever (grep for commit-mutex/task_claim/git in that file returns nothing). So the write path and the commit path are on two different locks, which is to say on no shared lock at all. The evictor claims the mutex, reads a file a peer is actively editing outside that mutex, runs its transform, and then git add at line 415 stages the ENTIRE current file content — eviction delta and peer WIP indistinguishably fused — and commits it under a cold-evict message. The peer WIP is captured not because the commit was sloppy about paths but because it was correct about paths and the harm lives inside one of them.
ready.secondary_latent_defect: SEPARATE AND ALSO REAL, BUT NOT THE OBSERVED CAUSE — DO NOT CONFLATE THEM IN THE FIX OR THE REPORT: line 416 is a BARE git commit with no pathspec after the line-415 git add. A bare commit commits the whole index, so any path a peer had staged would also be swept. That did NOT happen in e3e5c9f92 (one file changed, verified). ready.title: chef 07-21 morning dish self-certifies quality_verdict=full / layers 1-6 while its own persisted us_macro_layer has no PMI and no EFFR-IORB and known_gaps carries zero L2 token — the verdict gate is a narrative self-judgement, not an assertion over the payload it just wrote; FALSE certification, worse than an honest degraded
ready.note:
PO TRIAGE 2026-07-21 (TNB c115 finding F-CHEF-MORNING-FALSE-FULL-VERDICT). VERDICT: CONFIRMED AT SOURCE by PO — with ONE correction to TNB's evidence chain (below). This is a FALSE CERTIFICATION, which is a strictly worse failure mode than every previously-tracked chef finding: all prior ones were HONEST degraded self-reports.

RAW EVIDENCE (PO read docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-morning.json directly; note the fields are NESTED — metadata.* and tnb_synthesis.* — a top-level jq query returns null and will look like a missing field):
- metadata.cycle_id = "morning-2026-07-21T05:20:19Z"
- metadata.quality_verdict = "full"
- metadata.layers_walked_summary = "1-6 (full)"
- tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer = "Fed funds rate 3.63% with risk-off sentiment signaled by gold spike +$24.1 to $4053/oz. Safe-haven demand reflects caution amid margin debt expansion."  -> Fed funds ONLY. NO PMI. NO EFFR-IORB spread. Both are mandatory Layer-2 content per tnb-methodology.md / the main.md Layer table.
- known_gaps = ["[gap:business_context_sparse] ...", "[gap:gold_4300_active] ..."] -> ZERO L2 gap token.
So the dish certifies 6/6 layers walked while its own persisted payload shows Layer 2 is not walked, and emits no gap token to compensate. The quality signal is not merely wrong, it is confidently wrong — downstream consumers that trust quality_verdict to gate use have no way to detect this.

*** CORRECTION TO TNB'S EVIDENCE (PO re-verified; do not carry TNB's version forward) ***
TNB's finding argues the self-scoring gate CAN work by contrasting the SAME-DAY eod dish, which it says "explicitly tokens [gap:L2_US_macro_absent]". That contrast is NOT RAW-verifiable: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-eod.json DOES NOT EXIST (PO ls-confirmed; TNB's OWN other finding, GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A-FLOW-PERSIST, states the same file is Glob-confirmed absent). TNB therefore cited the eod NOTEBOOK claim as if it were persisted-JSON evidence, in the same handoff where it correctly reports that JSON never landed — an internal contradiction.
The proof leg SURVIVES, but must be re-anchored to the EVENING dish, which PO verified RAW: unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-evening.json has metadata.quality_verdict="degraded" AND tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer="EFFR-IORB spread 1.64pp NEUTRAL. Brent +2.31% ... Gold +1.97% ..." — i.e. genuine L2 content and an honest verdict, same agent, same day. That is a sound same-day control and it establishes the same point: the defect is isolated to the morning cycle, not universal.
CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS: do not build the fix around a comparison with the eod JSON. It is not there.

OCCURRENCE COUNT = 1 (first live-verified). Below the 3-cycle auto-cure threshold, and PO agrees auto-cure is the WRONG instrument here regardless of count — see the sibling row below.

FIX SHAPE (PO directive): the verdict gate must be a DETERMINISTIC ASSERTION, not a narrative self-judgement. Before writing metadata.quality_verdict="full", the agent must assert per-layer that the layer's own payload field is non-empty AND contains its mandatory tokens (L2: PMI and/or EFFR-IORB). If an assertion fails, "full" is not writable — the verdict must downgrade to "degraded" and a [gap:L<N>_...] token must be appended to known_gaps. Verdict and gap-token must be derived from ONE evaluation so they cannot disagree.

AC: (1) quality_verdict="full" is unwritable when any mandatory layer field lacks its required tokens; (2) verdict and known_gaps are computed from a single pass (no independent second judgement); (3) negative control — a synthetic dish with L2 stripped must produce degraded + an L2 gap token, proving the assertion fires (without this the fix is indistinguishable from always writing degraded); (4) RAW-verify on the next morning fire by reading metadata.quality_verdict + tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer from the persisted JSON — an agent self-report or notebook line is NOT acceptable evidence (the 07-21 morning notebook line matched the false "full" verbatim, so the notebook faithfully reproduces the bad verdict and cannot detect it).

SIBLING / DO NOT MERGE: FIX-CHEF-L6-TOKEN-PERSISTENCE-RECURRING (P3, BLOCKED) is the nearest prior art and is RELATED BUT DISTINCT. That row = a token WAS generated and then dropped on JSON write (persist-step vs narrative-gen, isolation-first, 3 manifestations despite 2 auto-cures). THIS row = no token was ever generated AND the verdict was affirmatively certified "full". Different mechanism, opposite end of the pipeline. They share the family "chef self-scoring integrity" and should be looked at together, but merging them would bury a false-certification bug inside a persistence bug. The L6 row's own lesson applies here though: more same-shape auto-cure is the wrong move; this needs a deterministic assertion.

ready.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T17:35Z by po as the ADJUDICATED UNBLOCKER for FIX-COVERAGE-SWEEP-BLANKET-STAMP-DEAD-TRIGGER (review/P1), which is COMPLETE-BUT-INERT: a 313-line deterministic script with 29/29 green tests that neither agent that must call it can invoke. Full reasoning, the three rejected options and the premise correction live on that row's `po_transport_ruling_20260725T1735` field — READ IT BEFORE EDITING ANYTHING. Do not re-litigate the choice here.

THE CHANGE — exactly two lines, no more:
  .claude/agents/news-scout.md:5      tools: Read, Write, Edit, mcp__gateway__call_tool   ->   tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, mcp__gateway__call_tool
  .claude/agents/market-watcher.md:5  tools: Read, Write, Edit, mcp__gateway__call_tool   ->   tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, mcp__gateway__call_tool

DO NOT also add Glob or Grep. The resulting grant set is exactly `Read, Write, Edit, Bash, mcp__gateway__call_tool` — the same shape fb-market-poster already carries, plus Edit. Any broader set is out of scope and should be bounced back to po.

WHY THIS IS NOT A POLICY BREAK (verified at source by po across all 43 .claude/agents/*.md frontmatter lines): fb-market-poster, a cowork PUBLISHER, already holds `Read, Write, Bash, mcp__gateway__call_tool`; system-auditor and orch-sentinel both hold Bash and both write shared state on cowork cadence. The originating report's claim that no-Bash is "deliberate fleet-wide policy shared by every cowork gatherer/publisher agent" is factually wrong — there are three standing exceptions in the same cadence tier.

WHY NOT AN MCP TOOL (the option that needs no grant at all): verified — docker-compose.yml does NOT mount ./scripts into the mcp-server container (mounts are ./data/live, ./data/pdfs, ./mcp.config.json, ./reports, ./docs/agent-memory, ./docs/data, ./docs/data/orch, ./docs/signals, ./docs/analysis-briefs, ./.claude/commands/crons). A `coverage_stamp` tool therefore could not exec the script; it would be a full TypeScript reimplementation of surgical-merge + task_claim mutex + --list-stale, i.e. a second implementation of one contract held in drift-lock with the first. Rejected on duplicate-implementation debt, NOT on feasibility (./docs/data is mounted RW, so it would work).

BLAST-RADIUS NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER — do not skip this, and do not treat it as a reason to refuse. Both agents already hold repo-wide `Write` and `Edit`, so an injected agent can already reach code execution transitively by rewriting a script a Bash-capable peer runs. Bash makes that direct rather than transitive. What is genuinely NEW is process execution and network egress (git push, docker, curl) from an agent whose input includes untrusted scraped news text. That is accepted here as proportionate to a live P1 coverage loss on a proven artifact, and it is the reason for the tight scope above and the non-precedent clause below.

NON-PRECEDENT CLAUSE (binding): this does NOT authorise Bash for the other 8 no-Bash agents (bctc-analyst, unified-agent, digest-predict, alert-commander, tran-ngoc-bau, market-analyst, refine_bctc_md, qa-responder). Each is a separate decision on its own merits. If a THIRD agent ever needs a scripted helper, stop granting per-agent and build the shared MCP transport at that point — the rewrite amortises across N agents instead of 2. That is the standing exit condition; no row is minted for it now because it is speculative.

LANE NOTE (deliberate, per the residual-gap lesson): minted into `ready`/READY rather than `backlog`, because next_agent=agent-father is a non-dev agent and a backlog row with a non-dev next_agent and no plan_only+supervised pair matches NO automated sweep lane (BOUNDED-1 requires next_agent =~ ^dev(-|$)|^developer$; SLS requires effective_supervised AND effective_plan_only). Such a row survives only on someone noticing. `ready` is dispatched explicitly by the router, which is the intended path here.

review.title: Debian->Ubuntu Dockerfile rebase silently reverted ALL of task-1779c SSH infra (openssh-client + ENTRYPOINT known_hosts seeding); entrypoint.sh has been tracked dead code ever since — restore it instead of weakening StrictHostKeyChecking
review.po_ruling_accept_new: PO RULING on the accept-new question. (1) REJECT `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` as the DURABLE answer — its stated justification is factually false. (2) KEEP it for now as a stopgap: reverting to `yes` today would simply re-break the tool, and nothing can be verified while the VPS is unreachable. (3) The durable fix is to RESTORE what already existed and was already QA-approved, then put `yes` back. This is un-reverting, not new design.
review.evidence: git b741c5634 (merge of 1779c, 'QA APPROVED', 2026-04-30) — apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile contained BOTH `openssh-client` (line 23) and `ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]` (line 63). git 6165aa3b4 ('fix(docker): rebase Dockerfiles from Debian to Ubuntu to unblock builds') — BOTH GONE, with no mention in the commit message. apps/mcp-server/entrypoint.sh is still tracked and clean at HEAD but is COPY'd/referenced by NOTHING (`git log -S entrypoint.sh -- apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile` after the rebase = empty). So the premise 'this could never have succeeded since inception' is inverted: it was correctly configured at inception and was silently regressed by an unrelated Dockerfile rebase ~2.5 months ago.
review.why_accept_new_is_weaker_than_claimed: The sshExec.ts comment claims accept-new 'STILL rejects a CHANGED key on any later connection'. That protection is largely illusory HERE: docker-compose.yml mounts nothing at /root/.ssh, so known_hosts is ephemeral per-container. Every `docker compose up` starts with an EMPTY known_hosts, so it is trust-on-first-use on EVERY container recreate, not once — a MITM need only win the race after any restart, and restarts are routine (the container restarted twice today). TOFU-on-every-boot is materially weaker than the one-shot TOFU the comment describes.
review.also_rejects_the_other_objection: dev-mcp-server rejected build-time keyscan partly because it 'hardcodes the VPS IP'. The VPS IP is ALREADY hardcoded in docker-compose.yml in four places (VPS_HOST plus three proxy URLs), so this costs nothing new. Its second objection — that it couples the IMAGE BUILD to VPS reachability — is valid, and is exactly why the existing entrypoint.sh does the keyscan at CONTAINER START, not at build.
review.scope: (1) Restore `COPY apps/mcp-server/entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh` + `RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh` + `ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]` to apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile. (2) Revert sshExec.ts to StrictHostKeyChecking=yes ONCE seeding is live and proven. (3) Add a regression test asserting the Dockerfile still wires the entrypoint, so a future rebase cannot silently drop it again.
review.mandatory_change_do_not_restore_verbatim: entrypoint.sh as written is `set -e` + `exit 1` when ssh-keyscan yields nothing. Restoring it VERBATIM while the VPS is unreachable would make the mcp-server container FAIL TO BOOT — turning a VPS outage into a total outage of all 88 crons and the whole MCP tool surface. It MUST be changed to degrade non-fatally: log a loud WARN, leave known_hosts unseeded, let the server start, and let only the SSH-dependent tools fail loudly at call time. A VPS-reachability problem must never be able to prevent mcp-server startup.
review.acceptance: Container boots with the VPS unreachable (WARN, no crash); with the VPS reachable, known_hosts is seeded at startup and `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` SSH succeeds; a Dockerfile-wiring regression test is green.
review.note: Shares a failure mode with FIX-CRON-SSCCHECKERJOB-DEAD-87D: work that was completed and signed off, then silently stopped being live, with no alarm — see that row's shared_failure_mode field. Also note reports/TASK_REPORT_1779c.md ticks `[x] Dockerfile: ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]` as satisfied; the checkbox is now false and nothing ever re-checked it.
